infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value: ATTACKS build up BLEED on enemies (25)

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 1x Abyssal Spine, 3x Shrapnel, 3x Swamp Thread, 3x Adhesive, 4x Vault Shard

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 5 / 59 - 103 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 76 - 133 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 94 - 164 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 112 - 196 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 130 - 227

description:
The abysmal whip is a power level 4 one-handed melee weapon that can be created at a blacksmith's bench. The recipe, Abyssal Remains, can be acquired by killing an Abyssal Demon. It can be ascended at a mystic forge with ascension cores. Note, if you ascend the Abysmal Whip to power level 8, and upgrade it to the Abyssal Whip, it will be brought down to Power Level 7.
This weapon's special effect is that regular attacks also build up bleed, and after five rapid hits, it will proc 28 damage at power level 4 and 40 damage at power level 7, despite only listing 25 for each. As this weapon deals slash damage, compared to swords, its attacks are slightly slower but slightly harder; however, its forward lunge distance is much shorter, and since enemies are knocked back significantly by most attacks, they will often be knocked out of this weapon's combos. It also does not have increased block without a shield compared to other similar weapons.

(Journal) We've all heard of it. We've all wanted it... the Legendary Abyssal Whip! The fabled weapon that heroes and adventurers have been seeking for an age!

You have taken it one step further. You have asked the question, "How hard could it be to make your own?". All you need is a spine from an Abyssal Demon! It comes pre-segmented and it's made from some of the hardiest organic material known to mortalkind. You just need to kill the demon, twist the shoulder, sever a tendon, and Io - your very own Abyssal Whip... right? Wrong. 

Turns out, it's a bit more involved than you expected, and this "weapon" demonstrates that all too well.

Still, not all is lost. Perhaps there is a way, a method, to turn this... "thing" into something that lives up to it's legend.

description:
The abyssal whip is a power level 7 one-handed masterwork melee weapon that can be created at a blacksmith's bench. To create this, it requires the Abysmal Whip to be wielded when interacting with a dragonkin statue near the Fight Cave. It is located directly North, in the lava.

(Recipe location) To unlock the recipe, an Abysmal Whip must be wielded while interacting with the dragonkin statue located in the lava directly north of the Fight Cave entrance.

(Journal) The abyssal demon is a foul beast. A single one can massacre a village before the warning bell can even sound. Crafting a weapon from their remains symbolizes triumph against adversity or perhaps just hubris in its purest form. 

Infused with the hate of the demon, each whip crack generates unbearable pain. Victims find themselves overcome with suffering as the agony seeps into the wounds the whips leave behind.

It is said that the whip even feeds on that misery, growing stronger with each life taken. The hate imbues the weapon with a desire to inflict more pain, and it grows stronger each time such a wish is granted. Or, so the legends say.

Only one Wild Knight has ever chosen to wield the whip in vengeance against the demon for a fallen sibling. Her name is dust in the wind of history, but there are still creatures that hide in the shadows, afraid of the crack of her whip.

name: Adamant Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips forged from adamant.

description:
Adamant arrows are a power level 7 ammunition that are crafted at a fletching bench, and can be used to craft adamant barbed arrow, poisoned adamant arrow, and adamant fire arrow.

(Journal) There is a constant battle between fletchers and armour smiths to one up each other. The armour smiths craft armour from stronger, sturdier and harder materials, meaning arrows must be made of equally, or greater, sturdiness of materials to pierce through them.

The adamant arrow is a shining example of this eternal conflict. The metal is durable, powerful and deadly in the right hands, and pierces mithril, steel and lesser metals with almost mocking ease. Only adamant and greater quality armour stands a chance against them."

name: Adamant Barbed Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Lacerating arrows with barbed tips forged from adamant.

description:
Adamant barbed arrows are a power level 7 ammunition that are crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) There are moments in life where you just decide that something must be forced to suffer. These arrows are designed just for that. When your enemy aggrieves you so much that you want to rip and tear and bleed them to death, this is the arrow for you.

The Moon Garou do not use these arrows, even though they are aware of their construction. They consider it an unnecessary amount of suffering to inflict, when a well-placed shot is quicker and less dangerous for everyone else.

Bandits that take up these arrows soon find themselves mistrusted even by their fellow thieves.

description:
Adamant bolts are a power level 7 ammunition crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) Sturdy bolts of one of the most durable metals. Capable of piercing most armours with relative ease.

Have you considered what else those metal bars could be used for? You could create tools that would grow plants in these desolate lands. You could craft beautiful sculptures to bring joy to all who see them.

But, no, you went with murder spikes instead.

Though there are ruddy great dragons around the place, so I suppose it’s a fair plan.

(Journal) Moon Garou tradition gifts a young warrior with a blade when they reach adolescence. One of the elder family members takes an old weapon of theirs and melts it down, refining age, memories and experience into a new blade for the newest generation.

It is a great day of pride for a young warrior to be gifted their first blade, but a bittersweet for the old warriors as they give up the dreams of future battles, passing the torch to those who come after.

Adamant, being the strongest metal that the Moon Garou can access, is believed to hold the strongest memories and those lucky youngsters that gain such a blade often find themselves elevated to positions of great respect and authority.

description:
Adamant fire arrows are a power level 7 ammunition that are crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) Fire almost seems redundant beneath the scorching glare of the Umbral Sands corrupted sun, yet fire will always find a way to burn something, if you let it.

The shamans of ancient Moon Garou tribes believed that fire was intelligent, and alive, in ways that defied normal understanding. Some fires were good, gentle creatures, that would warm the hearth and banish the cold in the night. But other fires were cruel things, possessed of an overwhelming desire for destruction.

The danger, of course, is, like people, all fires have the potential to betray you. Which is why some hunters had the sense to make sure the fire was very far away from them, by launching it through the air at ludicrous speeds.

description:
The adamant greataxe is a power level 7 two-handed melee weapon.

(Journal) Big axes are always popular among the violent crowd. In the Umbral Sands, a gathering of warrior Moon Garou gathered to show off who had the larger axe. Whilst the obvious innuendoes dogged the experience, in truth it was a competition among blacksmiths to see who could create the most powerful blade for the warriors to wield.

The adamant greataxe was created to showcase the raw power of the metal, and it was used with great zeal against a contingent of rampaging kalphites on hot summer. Seven warriors strode into the hive, axes held high and for the first time in a very long time, seven warriors emerged mostly unscathed.

Now, the greataxe is considered a good luck charm by any warrior Moon Garou who are strong enough to wield one.

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A strong and massive blade made of adamant.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Adamant Bar, 5x Scorch Leather, 4x Desert Thread, 4x Gypsum Wax

description:
The adamant greatsword is a power level 7 two-handed melee weapon.

(Journal) Few foes can stand against a great big slab of metal, filed down to the keenest edge. The weight of a great sword applied tremendous pressure across the edge, meaning that victims of a swing tend to find themselves falling to pieces in the face of it… quite literally.

The adamant greatsword is stronger than most blades, with only a handful of other metals offering sturdier construction. It was forged first by the legendary hero, Connakt, a Moon Garou warrior of great regard. Massive was his frame, and so he required a similarly sized blade in battle. He wielded his greatsword in a single hand, terrifying all who stood before him.

Connakt, it is said, travelled beyond the Umbral Sands, and indeed beyond Ashenfall, though the legends on how he did so vary greatly. They say that he travelled far away, settled down somewhere and had a family.

His greatsword “Sgian ìm” was buried with him.

name: Adamant Mace

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: An adamant mace designed to crush your enemies.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 8x Adamant Bar, 8x Yew Logs, 4x Scorch Leather, 2x Gypsum Wax

description:
The adamant mace is a power level 7 one-handed melee weapon.

(Journal) The first adamant mace was not, as you might expect, used for battle. Rather it was a rolling pin used by the ancient matriarch known only as The Crone – a name she chose for herself, thinking it quite funny.

Her baking skills were so dire, that whatever she produced had the consistency of iron and was more durable than steel. So, she required a tool strong enough to fight back against her sturdy pastries. She commissioned a rolling pin of adamant metal, and she used it with great zeal to beat her baked goods into submission.

Though teeth would still shatter against her scones, there was an artistry there that none could deny. So it was that more people would create adamant rolling pins, until an angry chef beat her rude husband to death with it, and the first true adamant mace was born.

After that, Moon Garou would still favour an adamant rolling pin, but many a warrior would bring a mace into battle, just in case they were forced to face up against the crone’s pastries. Which happened more often than is reasonably explainable.

(Journal) Wherever there is a sea, there are pirates, and the desert sands are a sea of sorts. A contingent of young Moon Garou once created a combination of rats, sails and a dash of magic, to create a sort of sand-ship, which they intended to use in acts of glorious buccaneering across the umbral desert.

They equipped themselves with scimitars of adamant, as it most closely resembled the cutlasses they’d heard about from human stories that had been stolen during the garou wars centuries past.

With eye-patches, golden teeth and an overzealous use of a particular consonant these youths set forth to become legends. Or they would, if their ship hadn’t immediately capsized and their mothers called them all back for tea.

The Moon Garou know the power of a good sword. They took the metal of the desert, with it’s green hue and unyielding nature and they turned it against the monsters of the sands. Beasts, great and powerful, fell to these weapons, entire legions of deadly creatures cut down in the dunes.

name: Adamant Warhammer

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A heavy warhammer forged from adamant.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 16x Adamant Bar, 3x Scorch Leather, 4x Gypsum Wax

description:
The adamant warhammer is a power level 7 two-handed melee weapon

(Journal) A little know tradition among Moon Garou blacksmiths, is to gather up all the bits of scrap metal from their workshops and create from them little figurines. They then sit beneath the shade somewhere, with various paints and turn these tiny creations into little pieces of art.

That was, until, Thraag learned of the game. Thraag was a blacksmith only so much in that he liked seeing metal melt. Something about the glow, the heat and the sheer sturdiness of the cooling metal, filled him with a sense of pride he never put into his personal hygiene.

Reeking like some unholy nightmare, Thraag was never invited to the gatherings of other blacksmiths, and over time the slight of being shunned festered within him, slowly mutating into something nasty.

He crafted a great hammer of pure adamant, sturdier and heavier then any hammer ever crafted before and he brought said hammer to the blacksmith gathering. There are few sights quite so tragic as grown blacksmiths weeping over smashed figurines.

It certainly did nothing to improve Thraag’s social standing.

name: Adventurer's Longbow
description:
The adventurer's longbow is a power level 2 longbow which can be crafted using a crafting table. The recipe is learned by consuming the vestige: a simple broken bow, found in a chest inside of Finn's Cave.

(Journal) The expedition to Ashenfall included skilled adventurers. If fate had been kinder, they could have gone down in legend as mighty heroes, rather than a slow, quiet,[sic] death where their names might be forgotten.

This bow was a design brought to Ashenfall by the hunter, Finn; a simple longbow crafted from easily obtained materials. Finn was a scout and a ranger who enjoyed getting into all the nooks and crannies of White Wolf mountain, in search of treasure. He joined the expedition in the hope of discovering new wonders and new stories to share with his people back home.

Instead, he found a dragon and the end to his story.

description:
The Ancestral Staff is a Power level 8 magic weapon. it can be crafted at a Mystic Forge using 12 Magic Logs, 6 Harmonised Compound, 2 Vis Cloth, 3 Dragonstone, and 2 Draconic Vis Wax

(Journal) Avisk weighed the staff in his hands. The Kobalios he had killed lay on the ground beside him, deflating into a pool of anima. Like a waterskin purged of its contents, he thought.

The Kobalio's staff fascinated him greatly. He knew that he was standing here, holding it, in this chamber of the Wellspring. But he couldn't shake the sensation that he was somewhere else, too. There was two of him, somehow; one here, and one not here.

Avisk knew of a sensation called 'phantom limbs', where one could lose a limb, from an accident, perhaps, but still feel that the limb was present. It was an adequate description for what he was feeling now: except, he felt like his body was elsewhere, and he was its phantom mind.

Avisk dropped the staff and the sensation dropped with it. A grin spread across Avisk's face. Oh yes, this was a discovery that deserved some investigation.

name: Ancestral Wand

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Forgotten magic lingers within this wand, waiting for a capable hand to awaken it.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 8x Magic Logs, 5x Harmonised Compound, 2x Vis Cloth, 2x Dragonstone, 2x Draconic Vis Wax

description:
The Ancestral wand is a power level 8 magic weapon. It can be crafted at a mystic forge using 8 magic logs, 5 harmonised compound, 2 vis cloth, 2 dragonstone, and 2 draconic vis wax.

(Journal) Holly Arnuld , the famed 'wand wizard', only had one blood relative, yet she found out about this relative's existence entirely by accident.

Frustrated at final-year students stealing her wands, Holly determined to discover a failsafe. She would create a spell that would respect the Bond of Blood: a spell that could be applied to her favourite wands to ensure only she used them. If someone without her blood tried to hold her Ancestral Wand, for example, then they would feel a burning pain.

The magic worked, but not quite as intended. 'Perfection is the enemy', as she would say. Her Ancestral Wand was bound to Arnuld blood, but it had not chosen Holly as the one who should wield it. There was another Arnuld out there, in the wilds, and the Ancestral Wand stubbornly decided that it belonged to THEM.

Holly hated that the next step was borrowed from a child's fairy tale, but there was no other choice. She invited people to come up and try to hold the wand. If they could do so without feeling pain, then she would recognise them as a relative and bequeath half of her estate. Hundreds of townsfolk tried, until a young orphan held the wand with no after-effect. Holly took her under her wing. The Ancestral Wand had a new owner.

Holly Arnuld tinkered with the Bond of Blood spell over the years, creating a variant that would eventually be used in her memorial chamber: Arnuld's Sanctum.

name: Ash Battlestaff

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A magical weapon carved from ash wood.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Ash Logs, 6x Rune Essence, 2x Coarse Thread

description:
The ash battlestaff is a power level 2 magic weapon. It can be created at a crafting table using 12 ash logs, 6 rune essence, and 2 coarse thread. Unlocked after building Spinning Wheel.

(Journal) It's not entirely clear why a staff helps channel magic. Druids would claim that it was because they were working with nature, aligning the magic spell through the plant's systems. Members of the Wizard's Guild argued that it wasn't that the wood itself was special but that they worked as a focus, helping to channel the mind of the wizard.

The inclusion of rune essence in a staff's design is a testament to the meticulous craftsmanship and artistry involved. This essence, often crushed into a fine powder and dispersed throughout the wood's careful grooves, creates a magical circulatory system within the staff. In this way, the staff becomes a living entity, with the wizard as its beating heart, channelling power through its veins to unleash upon foes. 

A staff is rarely helpful for less violent magic. They are brute force weapons, where magic is forced into elemental blasts, obliterating the target. More subtle spells rely on the caster's will and are powered directly by their magical skill.

name: Ash Shortbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A shortbow carved from ash wood.

description:
Ash shortbow is a power level 2 Shortbow that can be crafted at a Crafting Table.

(Journal) An Ash Shortbow is the first weapon most young archers train with. It’s easy to make and, therefore, not so problematic if it breaks during training. Human villagers would often craft their first bows together under the tutelage of a visiting Wild Knight. They would use branches that had naturally fallen from the trees and carefully whittle them into the bow’s limbs. Bowstrings would be created by gathering flax from the nearby fields and spinning it into thin but hardy threads. 

Most would break on first use. Some would break before the first arrow was fired. Still, village youngsters would laugh at their misfortunes and start the whole process again. Each time improving. Each new bow sturdier than the last.

name: Ash Wand

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A simple wand carved from ash wood. Every mage starts somewhere.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 6x Ash Logs, 3x Rune Essence, 1x Coarse Thread

description:
The Ash wand is a power level 2 magic weapon. It can be crafted at a crafting table using 6 ash logs, 3 rune essence, and 1 coarse thread.

(Journal) In Brynmoor, the wand will forever be associated with Holly Arnuld. She applied to every wizard to become their apprentice, but was turned down on account of her having a single arm. She would craft runes and concoct potions, displaying her skill and speed - faster than most other apprentices. The wizards would fill their eyes with pity and put a hand to her shoulder. "But can you hold a staff, lassie?", they would say. "I need to know that I can rely on you for all things."

Holly would not wield a staff. She believed them to be showy and unnecessary. They were as performative as a peacock's tail. Instead, she kept a sliver of staff in her sleeve. This was her ash wand, discretely socketed and ready.

She found work as a scullery maid for a noblewoman. She was travelling in their entourage when they were attacked by enough goblins to overwhelm the guards. The goblins were on the brink of killing the noblewoman when Holly pulled her wand from the stitching in her sleeve. She whipped the goblins from their feet with air magic. Every time they tried to get back on their feet, she put them to the floor again. They stumbled and stood, stumbled and stood, until finally she tumbled them off a cliff.

Holly was given a full purse and the contacts of a friend of the nobelwoman. She was enrolled in a school of magic. Her specialism? Well, she put all her efforts into the merit of wands.

name: Black Greataxe

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A hulking greataxe made from black metal.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 16x Black Metal Bar, 5x Maple Logs, 6x Cursed Leather, 32x Infernal Fragment

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 7 / 176 - 308 / 66 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 206 - 361 / 72 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 236 - 413 / 79

description:
The black greataxe is a power level 6 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. The recipe is unlocked after studying the bloodstained hilt, which can be purchased from Postie Pete's Evil Emporium for 300 infernal fragments, or acquired from chest (dowdun reach). It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is 4-7% increased damage compared to other greataxes at similar power levels, but it has the same 15% increased stamina cost as thane's authority.
This makes it flatly better than thane's authority, but unless it hits certain enemy breakpoints (i.e. killing an enemy in two hits instead of three), it may not be better than a mithril greataxe or adamant greataxe.

(Journal) Black metal was most commonly used for armours, crossbows and swords. On occasion, it was used for a greataxe. The reason is not a pleasant one. They were almost exhaustively the tool of an executioner, when the crime merited a public execution. The black metal was a message: you have betrayed the Children of Shadows, and your death will come from the metal of our own.

name: Black Sword

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A sword in the style of the Black Knights, forged from black metal.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 10x Black Metal Bar, 5x Cursed Leather, 4x Mystic Thread, 2x Demonic Oil

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 7 / 92 - 166 / 66 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 108 - 196 / 72 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 125 - 226 / 79

description:
The black sword is a one-handed power level 6 melee weapon. The recipe is unlocked after studying the shattered black blade vestige, which can be found in chests throughout Dowdun Reach or purchased from Postie Pete's Evil Emporium for 300 infernal fragments. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect deals 15% increased damage against mages, which includes garou druids, skeletal necromancers, zamorakian acolytes, and mages of zamorak. The latter two are also weak to slash damage, dealing an additional 25%, for a total of 44% increased damage.
This weapon has the same damage ranges when the same power level as the wooden training sword, but the toktz-xil-ak has slightly higher damage values in addition to having an additional chance to crit. The zombie axe also deals slash damage, but though it does more per hit, it uses the mace attack style which is slower. Therefore, this weapon is the ideal choice against mages, the toktz-xil-ak is best against other enemies weak to slash damage, otherwise the zombie axe is best in every other situation.

(Journal) Where the mithril crossbow is the standard issue of the ranged Black Knight, the black sword is standard for footsoldiers.

'Black', you may be aware, is not a material. It is instead a descriptor for steel that has gone through a process similar to vulcanisation. There was a time when the vulcanisation was performed by the dragon Xikotal, as a gift to the isolationist knights.

With his death, the process moved towards the demonic. The resulting quality is lower, which has made the original, dragonfire 'black' metal sought after in Dowdun Reach.

name: Blightwood Battlestaff

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A magical weapon fit for a Wizard.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Blightwood, 6x Wild Anima, 3x Swamp Thread, 4x Vault Shard

description:
Blightwood battlestaff is a power level 4 two-handed staff that can be crafted with a mystic forge.

(Journal) The stranger the wood, the more powerful the magic. It’s uncertain why this is, but it’s been true since magic was first discovered. When used as a tool for destructive magic, garou druids learned the power of blightwood. 
Ashien, a legendary druid among the garou, was among the first to wield such a weapon. As the story goes, they were wandering the swamps when the goddess Lougrim came to her in a vision and gave her a quest. Ashien was to journey deep into the swamps and do battle with a demon that dwelled[sic] within. 

They found the demon; it emerged out of the fog with a chilling screech and destroyed their staff with a single swing of its blade-like claw. In panic, Ashien blindly reached for the nearest weapon, the root of a swamp tree that had fallen in the mud. Through it, she channeled their will to survive and it burst free of the branch as a flash of lightning. 

The creature burned beneath Ashien’s gaze, vanishing back into the mists as if it never were. 

Since then, garou druids would favour blightwood when crafting a staff.

name: Blightwood Longbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A finely crafted longbow, powerful and precise.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Blightwood, 6x Swamp Thread, 4x Iron Bar, 4x Jade, 4x Vault Shard

description:
Blightwood longbow is a power level 4 Longbows that can be crafted at the fletching bench, once the recipe is unlocked by cutting and picking up blightwood and swamp thread.

(Journal) The wild creatures of Ashenfall have always been elusive. Bramblemead villagers would tell wild stories about the deer that got away or the sheep that shrugged off an arrow. Still, those who could wield a bow rarely left their family hungry. 
One Wild Knight, Frode, was so skilled with the bow that he never returned from a hunt empty-handed. His siblings among the Wild Knights would send him out hunting before every great gathering, so that they might feast heartily upon his return. For years, this was their happiest tradition. 

Until the day he did not return. 

It is said that his body was found in five separate places, spread out across the forests of Brynmoor like some gruesome compass. His quiver was empty, yet none of his arrows – marked as they were, with his symbol, an owl – would ever be found.

name: Blightwood Shortbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A finely crafted bow, fast and reliable.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 8x Blightwood, 3x Swamp Thread, 1x Iron Bar, 1x Jade, 4x Vault Shard

description:
The blightwood shortbow is a power level 4 Shortbow that can be crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) Every hunter reaches a crossroads in life when a choice becomes clear. They have honed their skills with a bow, surpassing the challenges posed by Brynmoor game. They could settle into a comfortable life in the village — hunting the same old deer, earning a regular wage and basking in a relaxing level of respect from their peers. Or, they could dare to dream bigger, to push their skills to new heights. 
The Wild Knights journeyed into more dangerous territories, facing off against deadly monsters warped by the anima twist. Joining them would mean abandoning the comfortable life of friends and family but earning a chance to face challenges that they would never face at home. 

Most choose comfort, as one might expect. But those who choose to improve would be taught how to craft a more powerful weapon, casting aside the oak bows that carry their names. They would carve a new name and identity into the limbs of their latest weapon and join the knights. Their names would be whispered. Gossip about them would transform into fireside stories — ghost tales about those still alive — the first embers of legends.

name: Blightwood Wand

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Fashioned from blightwood, its magic feels unsettlingly eager to obey.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 6x Blightwood, 3x Wild Anima, 2x Swamp Thread, 2x Vault Shard

description:
The Blightwood wand is a power level 4 magic weapon. It can be crafted at a mystic forge using 6 blightwood, 3 wild anima, 2 swamp thread, and 2 vault shard.

(Journal) Holly Arnuld travelled the world in search of materials for her wands. She would freely talk about the misadventures - making wands out of jade vines, for one - but would rarely talk about her successes. It was hard to know whether she was humble or unwilling to reveal her secrets.

One of those misadventures was in Bloodblight. She found a tree in the swamps with twigs that looked uncannily like wands. She wouldn't need to process the twigs much beyond snapping them from the tree. They glowed with magic, as if already prepared for their role.

Holly would treat this as a lesson to her students: perfection is an enemy. If something is flawless then it is hiding its flaw from you. Holly plucked a wand-twig from the tree and weighed it in her palm. But she could not shake the wand: it was stuck there. She was cursed to hold it in her palm, presumably forever if the blightwood tree had its way.

Holly was a sage enough wizard to remove the curse eventually, but it took some weeks to arrive at the solution. In the intervening period, she taught her lessons with a stony-face, grumpy temper, and a blightwood wand in her palm. She would point it threateningly at any student who dared to glance at her curse.

name: Blurite Bolts
description:
Blurite bolts are power level 4 ammunition that can be fired with a blurite crossbow or higher. They are crafted at a fletching bench after unlocking the recipe with the vestige: azure metal contraption.

(Journal) It was Mittens that learned how to turn blurite into crossbow bolts. His pet, the blacksmith Gothren, had continued to rely on iron and bronze to get the job done, but Mittens had realised that there was great potential in this strange blue metal. He would ruin sand moulds, crafted by Gothren to forge blurite bars, making them appear as long thin strips. It took more ruined moulds than the cat had hoped for his owner to realise that blurite bolts would match their namesake crossbow.

Whether they were more effective, is of no value to a cat, appearance is, after all, everything.

name: Blurite Crossbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A crossbow made from Blurite, thought to be a myth.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Blightwood, 6x Swamp Thread, 1x Blurite Crossbow Limbs, 1x Jade, 4x Vault Shard

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 5 / 49 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 61 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 75 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 88 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 102

description:
The blurite crossbow is a power level 4 crossbow that can be crafted at a fletching bench. The recipe is learned after studying the azure metal contraption found in a chest in northwest Fractured Plains. It can be ascended at a mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is -25% Reload Duration, making it reload faster than other crossbows. It also lists -25% durability, but it has the same amount as an iron crossbow.
The dorgeshuun crossbow can only fire bone bolts, so if specifically wanting to fire metal or enchanted bolts, this is one of the best options to do so. The shadow crossbow's special effect is 15% increased damage to weakpoints, which is a multiplicative modifier when considering weakpoints, 3/3 ranged armour, and the amulet of glory, but it fires slower than normal crossbows, making it much slower than this or the dorgeshuun crossbow. One of the benefits of crossbows is the flinch they cause on each hit, and the faster crossbows will do that more often.

(Journal) For centuries[sic] alchemists have yearned to create gold. To transmute base metals into something pure and shiny. While gold is the goal, there are other, stranger metals, along the way, and what could be more bizarre than a bar of purest blue.

Blurite is defined by its colour. It’s in the very name. Yet it offers no real magical, or alchemical value beyond other metals. Artistic, perhaps, it was favoured by poets, bards and[sic] artisans of more eccentric tastes, but it still offered little in the way of superior weaponry.

That was until Gothren Actillian took a crack at it. He was an blacksmith[sic], obsessed with the less desired metals and materials. He would hunt for hours in the darkest caverns for slivers of blue, ignoring glittering silver and gold. To him the metal was special, radiant and[sic] beautiful. The hues generated a joy in him that he could not describe, and he longed to craft it into something befitting its splendour. He was delighted when he found the ore glittering away in a hidden dragonkin vault in Ghornfell's central region.

He was never any good with a sword, and his magical prowess wouldn’t frighten a kebbit. Yet crossbows, those he could wield. He was a skilled marksman, and could knock an apple from a chinchompa’s head before it exploded.

The crossbow, blue as the ocean, caused much mockery from his companions, yet their mockery soon died as he speared a bolt through the heart of a dragon. Something all of their weapons had failed to do.

He was just disappointed that the dragon’s scales were green and went searching for that ever elusive blue.

name: Bone Bolts

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Lightweight, but very sharp. Can be fired using the Dorgeshuun Crossbow.

infobox.label: Special action
infobox.value: HITS cause BLEED build up on targets

description:
Bone bolts are a power level 5 ammunition that can only be fired from Dorgeshuun crossbows. Bone bolts are unlocked after completing the quest, Even More Restless Ghosts. Unlike other bolts that split their damage between the crossbow and the bolt, all of it is on the crossbow so that it ascends properly.

(Journal) Special bolts whittled from bones. Whilst only of use for a very specific crossbow, these bolts pack a surprising amount of punch.

name: Bone Club

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A primitive weapon made from bone, perfect for smashing other bones.

description:
The bone club is a power level 2 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a crafting table. Its special attack is a small leap with an overhead slam, dealing moderate damage.

(Journal) Animal bones are surprisingly durable, especially those found on Ashenfall. The magic of the continent seeps into their marrow, slowly strengthening them and making them tougher. This goes some way to explaining the ferocity of ordinarily docile creatures, but it also helps when crafting tools. 
Cows and similar beasts were celebrated in the age of Guthix. The people of Brynmoor preferred to take an animal’s life only on the hunt or after long years of service. When an animal passed, it was thanked for its sacrifice, and the materials helped strengthen the village. 

A club forged of bone was a simple tool, but one that made defending the village much easier. Roving beasts were easily pushed back and the village was protected by the animal’s last gifts.

name: Bone Dagger

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A sinister weapon, crafted from the bones of fallen creatures.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 4x Small Animal Fang, 4x Animal Bone, 2x Coarse Thread

description:
The bone dagger is a power level 2 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a crafting table. Its special attack is a small dash forward, followed by an upward slash, and can be useful as a combo extension.

(Journal) Before he learned to use the bow, Ulv survived with simple daggers of bone. He lived outside the village, cast out for his silence and strange ways. Ulv did not follow the polite nonsense of human society, nor did he seem to care for their troubles. The boy was happy just to survive and whittle small carvings of animals from fallen branches. 
He hunted silently, using the daggers to slay small prey such as rabbits and chickens. He ate what he needed and sold the excess at the markets for enough coin to purchase simple clothes and tools. 

When he was thirteen, he was beaten by bandits and left for dead. But a Wild Knight found him and brought him to safety. Recovering in the knight’s home, Ulv would be taught how to use a bow, a skill he soon mastered. 

When a wolf attacked Bramblemead, this outcast slew it. Villagers thanked him for his bravery and asked him what he wanted as a reward. He refused their offers and asked only for the wolf’s skull in return. He fashioned it into a mask that he chose as a new face, one he wore away from the village that had spurned him.

name: Bow of Elidinis

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: This ancient bow is a relic of Elidnis: Goddess of the Moon, Rivers, Growth and Fertility.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- LUNAR RAIN:
Call down a BARRAGE OF ARROWS that fall like rain and deal DAMAGE over the TARGETED AREA, with a chance of spawning a WATER ORB.

- BLESSING OF ELIDINIS:
Arrows deal WATER DAMAGE. Kills with water arrows have a chance to drop WATER ORBS that provide HEALTH REGEN when picked up.

- PURITY OF THE MOON:
Cannot use POISON, BLEED and FIRE ARROWS.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Gold Bar, 12x Silver Bar, 8x Desert Thread, 4x Dragonstone, 4x Gypsum Wax

description:
The bow of Elidinis is a power level 7 masterwork longbow that can be crafted at a fletching bench. The recipe is received as a reward for completing the Mapping The Sands II quest. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its first special effect is Blessing of Elidinis, which makes arrows also deal water magic damage in addition to ranged damage. Kills with water magic have a chance to drop water orbs that provide some health and a little hydration when picked up. Its special action is Lunar Rain, which costs 6 stamina and deals water magic damage over the targeted area for a short time. This is considered a Magic attack rather than a Ranged one, providing Magic XP and benefitting from the lesser magic potion and 3/3 magic armour's set effect increasing the chance of getting critical strikes instead of Ranged XP and weakpoint modifiers. However, its other special effect is Purity of the Moon, which is supposed to prevent the use of barbed, poisoned, and fire arrows when using this bow. However, this does not work, and all of those arrows can be fired from this weapon.
Similar to the zombie axe, when using normal, barbed, or poisoned arrows, this weapon deals both ranged and water damage simultaneously. Unlike most other damage modifiers, this damage is additive, which means that attacking an enemy weak to one but resistant to the other will result in more damage done than expected, but less than an enemy neither weak nor resistant to either. However, when using fire arrows, the water damage is replaced with fire. When comparing this bow to the hunter stagbow against KotHaar specifically, it deals slightly more, but the stagbow fires slightly faster. Therefore, when not using Astral Rain, in all other situations, the hunter stagbow is the ideal longbow to ascend.

(Journal) She is known by many names, both here and in the deserts entire oceans apart from one another, yet to all of them she is a source of life and creation. She is the river in the desert sands, from which all civilisation blooms, and she is the rain that washes away the cruel and merciless when the monsoon season comes.
To the Moon Garou, she is the River Mother, the Moon Maiden, and their salvation. For it was she, who helped the wandering garou to step away from their primal predatory nature, and tame the sands, cultivating crops and building cities.

She left the deserts centuries ago, to places unknown. Some say she wanders the stars in search of a place where her grief can be lessened. While others claim she prepares for war against a more insidious foe. A creature of fire, ash and hatred, the demon of the sun.

This bow was left to one of her favourite Moon Garou, a warrior called Kyter, whom she raised as her own after he was orphaned by a cruel sandstorm. The bow was passed down his family line, parent to child, until the last of the bloodline was murdered by Fuzan.

Now, the bow is yours. Use it wisely, for she will surely be annoyed if you don't.

name: Bronze Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips forged from bronze.

description:
Bronze arrows are power level 3 ammunition that can be crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) Bronze Arrows offer greater armour piercing than their non-metallic counterparts. Copper and tin were relatively uncommon in Brynmoor, so using the resources on arrows seemed like a waste of money. One faction of bandits delighted in this premise; their leader, a man known as the Auburn Ocelot — for reasons he would never explain — took great amusement in their use. 

The Auburn Ocelot would laugh as his bandits hurled expensive arrows at the villagers, pilfering coins worth far less than the ammunition used to corral them. To him, it wasn’t about the money but the look of confused terror on their faces and the knowledge that no one could stop him. 

He was above it all. Better than everyone. 

It was a rat that killed him. Not even a giant one. Just a tiny creature carrying a virulent plague. Money could not save him, no matter how much he flaunted. He was cremated and his ashes buried in the middle of nowhere so that no one might risk catching the infection that cost his life. 

Now, he’s almost completely forgotten.

name: Bronze Barbed Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Lacerating arrows with barbed tips forged from bronze.

description:
Bronze barbed arrows are bronze arrows with weapon barbs crafted on the arrow. Targets that are hit by a bronze barbed arrow will be inflicted with the bleed debuff. Like other barbed arrows, the icon will have a bleed icon placed on the top right of the arrow to distinguish itself from regular arrows.

(Journal) The barbed bronze arrow was the ammunition of choice for the hunting party of Lord Gawurin, the regent of Ashenfall. He and his hunting party would head out into the woods alongside a small contingent of White Knight bodyguards. The lord would hunt deer, boars and other game there, but he wasn’t the most accurate shot.

This arrow was designed for bloodletting, meaning he only needed any hit to begin the prey’s downfall. A single strike would start them bleeding, slowing them down and making them easier to hunt. The hunt outcome was all but inevitable. Poor sport, some would whisper, but the lord cared only for the end result.

It’s perhaps fitting, then, that Lord Gawurin would be hunted with his own arrows on the night of Falling Embers.

name: Bronze Bolts
description:
Bronze bolts are a power level 3 ammunition that can be fired from bronze crossbows.

(Journal) Not a lot can be said about small spears of metal launched at high speeds into your opponent. They do exactly what you think they'll do to the target, and it's rarely pretty.

Guards would buy crossbow bolts in bulk from the village blacksmith, giving him a steady income. This sadly had the effect of making the village blacksmith the most burgled property around.

name: Bronze Crossbow

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Oak Logs, 6x Wool Thread, 1x Bronze Crossbow Limbs, 1x Opal

description:
A bronze crossbow is a power level 3 Crossbow that can be crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) The members of the Wild Knights who trained with melee weapons, generally found themselves the victors in friendly sparring matches against their companions. The reasoning was simple – shields. A shield could turn aside blade, arrow and spell, with equal skill[sic] and it left their enemy vulnerable to counterattack. This sense of superiority began to change from friendly competition, into a sense of smugness capable of souring many friendships.

Roliker Hallister was particularly obnoxious. His skill with sword and shield was admittedly impressive. At the age of twenty[sic] he could best even some of the commanders of the Wild Knights in single combat. Healthy pride twisted into smug egoism, which then rotted down into unpleasant superiority. He was rude. He was dismissive. He was pretty much an obnoxious nightmare to be around.

Which is why he was very surprised by the bolt in his shoulder, and why no one else seemed too inclined to help him out. Vanida Mox was a skilled archer and inventor. She was quick to learn, quick to study[sic] and she had the enviable ability to see when something was wrong and work to find a solution. Popular with the other knights, because she would work with them, share accolades, and stand for what the order truly meant – a barrier between the world and the wild.

As Roliker’s ego grew and grew, she realised that the archers in the order were at a significant disadvantage in close combat. At range, they were obviously superior, but as all the sparring matches were held in the courtyard, there was precious little distance available. So she began working on a device that would deliver the power of an arrow[sic] but allowing one hand free to hold a shield.

It was very effective.

She named it a “cross-bow”, because she was very [sic]very angry when she unloaded it into the cloud of smugness known as Roliker. Later[sic] that name would be attributes[sic] to the mechanical structure of the device, but now you know better.

name: Bronze Dagger

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A small blade forged from bronze, suitable for close combat.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 6x Bronze Bar, 3x Small Animal Fang, Wool Thread

description:
The bronze dagger is a power level 3 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a small dash forward, followed by an upward slash, and can be useful as a combo extension.

(Journal) Bronze is a common enough alloy, a combination of copper and tin. Durable, defiant, and deadly in the right hands. For Mia Larsdottir, it was a bronze dagger that pierced her heart, cutting her life short at the age of twenty-one. 
As the first of the Amalgamated, she had never expected to reach any of the milestones traditionally followed by her peers. She did not expect to be married and she never let herself dream of being a mother. She thought, perhaps, that she might be allowed to carve a quiet little place for herself, somewhere with room for cats. 

But a bronze dagger stole that dream from her. 

Her killer was never brought to justice, though there were rumours about who they were. Her father was the chief suspect, ashamed as he was to bring the first of the unnatural Amalgamated into the world. He denied it, of course, but he never held a funeral for her. Instead, her body was left in the forest, where nature might put her at peace.

name: Bronze Fire Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Burning arrows with tips forged from bronze coated in fire oil.

description:
Bronze fire arrows are bronze arrows with fire oil applied with level 45 Ranged. Targets that are hit by a bronze fire arrow will be inflicted with the burning debuff, damaging the enemy by 5% of their max health for six seconds. Like other fire arrows, the icon will have a fire icon placed on the top right of the arrow to distinguish itself from regular arrows.

(Journal) Deadly arrows made deadlier with fire. Each arrow burns with the fury reserved for the most unpleasant parts of Infernus. They sear, they singe, and they melt the flesh, turning their victim into little more than ashes floating away on the wind.

In the days of the great war against the Garou, the priests of Saradomin encouraged the use of these weapons. They saw it not just as a means of eradicating the hated beastmen, but to purify the world from their taint. Lougrim was a false goddess, in their eyes, and her followers had to be cleansed from existence.

Modern scholars would doubtless be confused at their monotheistic mindset, considering that the literal god of war, Bandos, walked beside them into battle. The mental gymnastics employed by the Brynmoor priesthood, could have rivalled any athlete in the Gielinor Games.

name: Bronze Greatsword

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A two-handed bronze sword for those who prefer power over speed.

description:
The bronze greatsword is a power level 3 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at the blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a large circular slash that lunges the player forward in the direction they are aiming, useful for hitting large groups simultaneously and changing directions during a combo.

(Journal) The Wild Knight, Kessel, was unusual in her choice of weaponry. Where most of the order chose to wield bows, daggers, or swift blades, Kessel favoured the Bronze Greatsword. On the battlefield, she hefted it across her shoulders, never letting the hilt leave her grip. 
As one of the Amalgamated, Kessel’s skin glowed like burning coals, her battle scars resembling faint reddish embers. She harnessed this heat, channelling it through her sword. Her magic set the blade ablaze, a sight that struck terror into the hearts of her enemies. With great arcs of red flame, she cleaved through enemy forces, incinerating them as she severed their limbs from their bodies. 

On one fateful day, she would use this technique against a force of garou hunters. The battle was long, hard and brutal, and both sides faced great casualties. But it was when she sliced her blade across the young garou prince that war was inevitable.

name: Bronze Mace

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Crush your foes with this heavy, spiked bronze mace.

description:
The bronze mace is a power level 3 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a small leap with an overhead slam, dealing moderate damage.

(Journal) The bronze guard defended the alliance between the followers of Guthix and the followers of Saradomin. The metal symbolised the unity of two different materials and created something stronger. While most of the guards preferred the noble sword, a few preferred the physicality of the Bronze Mace. 
Each swing delivered powerful momentum straight at the enemy. The force broke bone, obliterated muscle and often sent their victims reeling, allowing a second strike before the foe could recover. 

There was a mountain of a man known as The Cairn, for his skill at delivering people to one, who favoured the mace over more noble weapons. He crushed anyone who defied the alliance, providing the force of justice with each swing of the mace. 

When he was asked to turn his fury on the priests of Guthix, it was the one time he stayed his hand.

name: Bronze Sword
description:
The bronze sword is a power level 3 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a forward stab, which can reach quite far forward compared to most melee attacks, making it useful for combo extensions and intercepting an opponent before they can attack.

(Journal) Legend has it that when the first sword was forged, Guthix wept. Given that Guthix commissioned warriors and soldiers and, at times, encouraged war, this is perhaps not a truthful statement. Yet, the sword is a weapon with a singular purpose: to end the life of another. Of course, this is true of all weapons, but none are as iconic as the blade.
Children would play in the street, striking one another with wooden blades rather than clubs or daggers. They would pretend to be knights rather than brigands or priests. To wield a blade was a sign of bravery. To draw a sword was the hero's stance.

War shatters all childhood dreams.

Nothing removes the nonsense of chivalry more efficiently than seeing the life leaving the eyes of a terrified foe. A sword puts the wielder in that moment, forcing them to face that which they destroy; to understand that there are no such things as heroes:[sic] only warrior against warrior and the knowledge that one will fall.

name: Bronze Warhammer

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A heavy-hitting, two-handed weapon crafted from bronze.

description:
The bronze warhammer is a power level 3 two-handed melee weapon that is crafted at the blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a slow and heavy slam in front of the player, with a small area-of-effect shockwave that will cause a hard knockdown on most opponents and deal heavy damage.

(Journal) Doric would be the first person to praise the simple hammer. It is a large solid chunk of metal attached to a long haft, allowing the weapon to benefit from the unmistakable might of physics. Weight and speed are a terrifying combination. 

Dwarves, in particular, favour this weapon. They feel it speaks to their long-held desire to form metal by pounding it into shape by sheer strength alone. They apply the same logic to their enemies, beating them into a shape that the dwarves feel suits their enemies better. 

There were once dwarves on Ashenfall who were masters of this technique. However, when the humans began their infighting, and Guthix turned away from them, they vanished deeper into the continent in search of something extraordinary, leaving behind a shroud of mystery. 

They found what they sought and have never returned.

name: Chieftain's Blade

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: The sword of a goblin chieftain, used to spread war in the name of the Big High War God.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- INCREASED chance of landing CRITICAL Hits with SWORD ATTACKS

- Reduced DAMAGE

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 4 / 43 - 78 / 46 / Ascension Core (Power Level 4) 1; 5 / 58 - 104 / 52 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 73 - 132 / 59 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 90 - 162 / 66 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 106 - 192 / 72 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 123 - 222 / 79

description:
The chieftain's blade is a power level 3 one-handed weapon, created by combining 10 bronze bars, 2 antlers, and 2 animal bones at a blacksmith's bench. The recipe is learned by consuming the vestige a corroded serrated blade, found in a chest atop the same plateau where you start the Heartstrings quest. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
It has even lower damage ranges than the wooden training sword, making it the least valuable weapon to ascend.

(Journal) Mouldfinger never wanted to be chief, unlike the other goblins she aspired to be just a background character - happy and forgotten while she worked on her own things. She enjoyed working with wood, bone, and on those special occasions, metal.

She crafted a sword, a simple blade that was sturdy and strong, and the goblins went wild because of it. Seeing its sharpness, they became convinced it was magical or imbued with the power of their draconic overlord. it wasn't, it was just very well made.

She was made chieftain after the others challenged her, and her sharpened blade cut easily through their defenses. A fate she had never wanted, and a fate she would never escape.

name: Crystal Bow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A powerful Shortbow fashioned from crystal of elven origin.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 18x Opal, 4x Wool Thread, 4x Bronze Bar, 4x Anima-Infused Bark, 8x Vault Shard, 1x Vault Core

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 4 / 36 / Ascension Core (Power Level 4) 1; 5 / 46 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 58 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 70 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 82 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 94

description:
The crystal bow is a power level 3 masterwork shortbow that can be obtained (as well as its crafting recipe) as a reward from the Heartstrings quest. It can then be crafted at a fletching bench. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special attack is called Shattershot, costing 43 stamina and shoots an area-of-effect cone of arrows a short distance that deals one third of the weapon's base damage to every target hit. Each target hit is stuck with crystal needles that explode after a short time for a set 50 damage. More needles can be stacked before the previous set explodes. This special attack does not require arrows to fire and can penetrate solid objects.
This weapon fires slightly slower than other shortbows despite dealing very similar damage when at the same power level, even when compared to the undead ranger's bow which is supposed to have increased damage as its special effect. This weapon has the same durability as the other ascendable shortbows, which makes the wild scout's shortbow with its 10% faster draw speed the ideal choice of shortbow to ascend if not using shattershot.

(Journal) A Crystal Bow is not crafted but sung into existence. Harmonies are layered over one another to teach the weapon a story so that it might understand why it needs to be strong. Traditionally, the songs that are sung are of the plight of the elves, their loneliness without their goddess, and the many dangers they must face.

The shimmering substance they're made from is traditionally a shard of the elven goddess Seren, left behind when her crystal form shattered at the end of the Third Age God Wars.

This bow isn't of the same material, and the song is different, too. There's no divine essence in the crystal, no lament of the elves. Instead, it is sung memories of a lifetime together, distilled down into facets reflecting in the crystalline flaws. In the moonlight, those facets sparkle like tiny stars held within glass — moments of hardship, conflicts, happiness[sic] and grief.

It is music as a weapon, with memory as its handle and sorrow as its string.

name: Dorgeshuun Crossbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: The signature weapon of the Dorgeshuun Goblin tribe. It fires Bone bolts and is surprisingly well made!

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- Increased DRAW SPEED with RANGED ATTACKS

- Can only fire BONE BOLTS

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Willow Logs, 6x Swamp Thread, 1x Bone Crossbow Limbs, 1x Jade, 4x Vault Shard

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 6 / 122 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 149 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 176 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 203

description:
The dorgeshuun crossbow is a power level 5 crossbow that can be crafted at a fletching bench. The recipe is obtained from the quest Even More Restless Ghosts. It can be ascended at a mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is a hidden -25% Reload Duration, making it reload faster than other crossbows. It also can only fire bone bolts, which can similarly only be fired from this crossbow. Unlike other crossbows and bolts that split the damage between them, all of it is on the crossbow. This is to ensure that the weapon ascends correctly, and isn't forced to use weaker bolts than other crossbows. The bone bolts additionally build bleed, and with three hits in a short time, deal 40 damage. This damage does not scale with power level.
Excluding the bleed damage from the bone bolts, this weapon has the same base damage, reload speed, and durability as the blurite crossbow at similar power levels. With that in mind, the choice comes down to what bolts are desired, particularly enchanted bolts, as the difference is entirely down to their effects. The shadow crossbow is a notable mention as it can squeeze more damage out of enchanted bolts with +15% weakpoint damage, but it does so far slower than this or the blurite crossbow.

(Journal) The cave goblins are a practical sort, using materials more readily available underground than any that might require potential damage to their subterranean dwellings, such as mining. This crossbow is made from bones, traditionally of creatures found beneath the surface.

Zanik once used this crossbow to defeat a deadly spectre in the underworld. A being infused with some dread malign power, that threatened the denizens of Um. Normal weapons had no effect on the creature, yet for some reason the bone bolts fired by this crossbow were enough to unravel its material form, banishing it back to the darkness.

name: Draconic Staff

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: An ancient dragonkin staff used by the mages of old.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- Increased chance of landing CRITICAL HITS

- Reduced DURABILITY

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 10x Iron Bar, 6x Granite, 4x Jade, 4x Vault Shard

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 5 / 5.4 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 6.8 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 8.3 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 9.8 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1

description:
The draconic staff is a power level 4 staff that can be crafted at a mystic forge. The recipe is unlocked after studying the parts of a sinister-looking staff, which can be found in a chest on the western wall outside of Skeklac Kara, the dragonkin vault in Ashien's Watch. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is +15% critical strike chance which equates to an average 1.0375x damage increase, but it also has -15% durability. Unlike the dragonbone dagger, this weapon does have reduced durability compared to the blightwood battlestaff (its comparable weapon) which has 1300 to this weapon's 1100.
However, when compared to the staff of light and necromancer's staff at equivalent power levels, it always has a 0.4 - 0.5 lower rune damage multiplier. In order for the increased chance to crit to have a higher average damage increase, the rune multipliers would need to increase to higher than 12 while maintaining the 0.4 - 0.5 difference (in other words, this staff would need a rune multiplier of 12.3 and +15% critical strike chance to have the same average damage as the necromancer staff if it had a rune multiplier of 12.8).

(Journal) Rasthin was a powerful sorceress, even among the dragonkin. She had mastered all manner of spells and was even schooled in the techniques from the previous Revision.

Still, magic as an art was largely looked down upon by dragonkin society. It was considered vulgar and the obsession of children. Alchemy and science were the real way forward. In part, it’s because of the connection between magic and the hated Elder Gods, and the dragonkin feared rousing, further, their anger.

But Rasthin knew the value of magic, as did the other members of her group. She created a staff, forged from glittering crystal and anima-infused iron, which allowed her to channel her magic into powerful spells.

Yet, even with a weapon as powerful as this, she discarded her magic when she uncovered the power of Ashenfall – preferring, instead, to enjoy her newfound connection with elemental flame.

Still, the remnants of the staff pulse with potential, and while they may never reach the might of their former power, they remain mighty magic tools, just waiting to be crafted.

name: Dragon Crossbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: An exceptional crossbow crafted from dragon metal. The bolt arrives before the target realises it has been fired.

description:
The Dragon crossbow is a power level 9 ranged weapon that can be received after completing the Scorned Wilderness raid and opening the Queenslayer's Reward Pack. Unlike many other weapons in the game, this crossbow is both uncraftable and has a passive full durability.
Bug: Despite the special effect stating an increase to damage against dragons, this crossbow does not currently get a damage boost against dragons.

(Journal) Brakka presented the cache of weapons to the other dragonkin. For himself he chose the kiteshield: he didn't care much for combat, and he felt a strange kinship with its resilience.

Avisk chose a scimitar with a growl. He turned the metal in his hands and licked it. Brakka knew Avisk well enough that Avisk would be more interested in the material and its properties for his studies. Avisk chose the scimitar simply because it contained the greatest weight of the metal.

Rasthin was next and chose a crossbow and some bolts. She walked immediately to her workbench and began exposing the metal to the elements. She lit a bolt on fire and seemed satisfied that the fire failed to extinguish.

Lacrussa took a kiteshield. She tossed it to the corner, disinterested with these trinkets.

Brakka didn't know what to expect from Viika. He wondered whether they would turn down the gift, perhaps, or pick a kiteshield - something of a more pacifist bent.

Viika picked the dragon crossbow. "I know someone who will have need of this," they said.

name: Dragon Scimitar

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A razor-sharp dragon scimitar favoured by warriors who value speed as much as strength.

description:
The dragon scimitar is a Power level 9 weapon that can be received after completing the Scorned Wilderness raid and opening the Queenslayer's Reward Pack. Unlike many other weapons in the game, this scimitar is both uncraftable and has a passive full durability.
Bug: Despite the special effect stating an increase to damage against dragons, this weapon does not currently get a damage boost against dragons.

(Journal) Dragon metal is not, as the name might imply, made of dragons. Well, not directly. It's a composite of a material called orikalkum (or orichalcum, depending on whether you prefer to use the dwarven spelling) and drakolith, which no longer resides on Ashenfall. The dragonkin, notably Brakka, exhausted whatever deposits were left on the island.

Once an alloy has been formed by these two materials, it needs to be forged in dragonfire. That, unlike drakolith, was in abundance on Ashenfall. The result was dragon metal, and Brakka could make precious little of it. There was enough to make a throne, perhaps, or a motherlode maw. Realistically, Brakka couldn't use the metal to make much of material use, so he a forged small armoury of kiteshields, scimitars and crossbows. If the dragonkin were to ever be threatened, then they would at least have the best weapons on Ashenfall to respond.

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A ferocious blade, filled with primal draconic rage.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 6x Ram Horn, 3x Antler, 1x Hard Leather, 4x Vault Shard

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 5 / 38 - 98 / 52 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 48 - 123 / 59 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 59 - 150 / 66 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 69 - 177 / 72 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 80 - 204 / 79

description:
The dragonbone dagger is a power level 4 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. The recipe can be found in Chaktan Kara, the dragonkin vault in northwest Stormtouched Highlands. It can be ascended at the mystic forge with ascension cores.
Its special effect is +15% critical strike chance, which equates to an average 1.0375x damage increase. It also lists -15% durability, but it has the same amount of durability and does not deplete faster than the iron dagger. 
Although keris has 2 higher max hit at power level 7, this dagger when ascended has the same stats as the wolfbane dagger, and so when not attacking either kalphites or wolves, this is the ideal one-handed stabbing weapon to ascend.

(Journal) Viika was never fond of creating dragons, they thought the process was cruel and unbecoming. When an egg was laid, Viika saw in that moment both the egg and the dragon it would become. They saw past and presence[sic] at the same time, and they grieved the creature before it had even hatched.

They pleaded with their sibling, and with the other Dragonkin, to change their treatment of the beasts. But Viika’s curse, like so many Seers, was to be ignored by their kindred.

A rare egg hatched once, containing a dragon with white scales like pearls. The dragon was infused with magic and possessing[sic] a power capable of travelling to other worlds, where she might have lived a happier life. But Viika wept, for they knew she would manage no such ending.

Viika kept the hatchling company. Treated them like their dearest friend, and held them softly when Lacrussa’s need for knowledge, took the dragon’s last breath.

The Seer kept only a single keepsake – a blade carved from the tooth of their white-scaled friend. A dagger capable of terrible damage, but as fragile as the friendship that it reminded them of.

name: Enchanted Adamant Bolt

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Adamant bolts infused with sanguine energy and a ruby tip. Drains some of the archers health to increase the bolts damage.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 33x Adamant Bolt, 1x Ruby, 10x Astral Rune, 15x Fire Rune

description:
The Enchanted Adamant Bolt is a power level 7 bolt crafted at a Fletching Bench. It has a 15% chance to drain 15% of the user's current health and increase critical hit damage by 40% for that shot on a successful hit. If the special effect activates on a missed shot, the user's health is not drained, but it is still drained on non-critical hits.

(Journal) Adamant is a special metal, responding well to magic and allowing it to be shaped into durable and deadly forms. Adamant bolts are the bane of many creatures, their sharpness and their hardiness lets them pierce through almost any defence.

Yet, what if you didn’t stop the magic in the crafting process? What if you added more and more, creating bolts enchanted with murderous wrath? The answer to that is in these enchanted bolts, that sap your life in order to deal greater damage to your foe.

Sacrifice for vengeance, the gods would approve.

Except Guthix, but his opinion is somewhat moot these days.

name: Enchanted Blurite Bolts

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Blurite crossbow bolts tipped with enchanted Jade, that have a chance of dealing Earth magic damage and knocking your target down.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 33x Blurite Bolts, 1x Jade, 10x Astral Rune, 15x Earth Rune

description:
Enchanted blurite bolts are an upgradeable version of blurite bolts unlocked at level 35 Ranged. Upon creation, there is a 15% chance of the stack of bolts being enchanted with 10% earth magic damage.

(Trivia) When equipped, the description mentions slowing down the target; the enchanted blurite bolts knock the target down instead.

(Journal) No one is entirely sure who thought to enchant blurite crossbow bolts in Brynmoor. The earliest references talk about Ignatius Wormwood, a failed apprentice wizard with too much time on his hands.

The story goes that he was challenged by one of the Knights to a duel, over some spat about a maiden or other. Evidently [sic]Ignatius may have been a failure in his robes, but worryingly successful out of them, if you get my gist.

Now, the knight was a large and imposing man — referred to by his compatriots as the immovable boulder — and angry as he was, he had no intention of killing Ignatius, so he gave him a simple challenge instead. If Ignatius could knock him down, he’d win the duel, otherwise the Knight would claim victory and see Ignatius punished for his mischiefs.

When Ignatius pulled the crossbow from his robes, the knight was concerned but knew that his armour and shield could stand against them. Yet, when the bolt impacted the knight’s pristine iron armour, he found himself hurled to the floor and the wind knocked out of him.

Gracious in defeat [sic]the knight let Ignatius go, only for the wizard to wander into the next person he had wronged.

name: Enchanted Bronze Bolts

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Bronze crossbow bolts tipped with enchanted opal. These have a chance to summon a lightning strike around your target, dealing Air Magic Damage to all nearby enemies.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 33x Bronze Bolts, 1x Opal, 10x Astral Rune, 15x Air Rune

description:
Enchanted bronze bolts are an upgradeable version of bronze bolts unlocked at level 35 Ranged. Upon creation, there is a 15% chance of the stack of bolts being enchanted with 10% air magic damage and up to 16 damage towards the enemy via the Shocked debuff.

(Journal) Magic was never enough. Oh, sure, you could change bones into delicious peaches, you could summon water out of thin air, you could call down fire upon your foes and laugh as their flesh turns to ash (if you’re that way inclined). Yet, even so, it was never enough. There was always more death to deal, more damage to inflict, more pain to spread and the priests of Brynmoor wanted more of it.

They wanted to see the garou crushed. Wanted to see them begging as the last of their pups expired beneath Saradomin’s purifying flame. So, they commissioned the wizards and alchemists to find new and innovative ways to summon suffering.

Crossbow bolts proved to be an interesting revelation. By affixing gemstones to the tips of these weapons, not only could they inflict deadly wounds on their enemies, but they could also inflict debilitating pain so powerful that the opponent would be stunned, making the next attack much easier.

The priests were very happy with this discovery. The so called “heretics” within Brynmoor were less so.

name: Enchanted Iron Bolts

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Iron crossbow bolts tipped with enchanted Jade, that have a chance of dealing Water magic damage and slowing your target.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 33x Iron Bolts, 1x Jade, 10x Astral Rune, 15x Water Rune

description:
Enchanted iron bolts are an upgradeable version of iron bolts unlocked at level 35 Ranged. After creation, there is a 15% chance of one of the bolts being enchanted with 10% water magic damage.

(Trivia) When equipped, the description mentions knocking down the target; the enchanted iron bolts instead slow enemies down.

(Journal) Stone remembers, wood forgets, iron holds a grudge. So goes the Imcamdo saying. A reference to how much stronger metal weapons were than wood and stone. Still, with magic, this adage can become painfully true.

The first enchanted iron bolts on Ashenfall were crafted by Lina Hesperian, one of the Amalgamated. She had hair that flowered[sic] like a waterfall down her spine. Her eyes were crystalline lakes, sparkling in the light, and her smile was as refreshing as any spring. She enchanted the bolts so that they might carry the gift of water, washing away infection for a clean and gentle kill. She made them for the hunters, so that they might claim their quarries with as little suffering as possible.

She met the end that far too many Amalgamated suffered. Alone, frightened, in the cold and the dark of an alley, her blood seeping from the knife wound in her chest. As she gave her last breath, she cursed the world for it’s cruelty, and the iron listened.

Now, each enchanted iron bolt taps into that grudge, inflicting a reminder of her suffering on any that feel the bolt’s sting.

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: These crossbow bolts offer a chance to create a toxic burst, poisoning all nearby enemies.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials

description:
Enchanted mithril bolts are a power level 6 ammunition crafted at a fletching bench that has a 15% chance to create a toxic burst, poisoning all nearby enemies within a 4-5 meter radius.

(Journal) Goodness, you must really want to kill someone. As if punching through their armour with a crossbow bolt wasn't enough, you want to magically scupper them too. Remind me not to get on your bad side.

When the special effect activates, the shot also pierces enemies. Despite being power level 8, these bolts deal the same base damage as Enchanted Adamant Bolts.

(Journal) You can argue the semantics, but rune is already enchanted. It has inherent magical properties, which means that 'enchanting' it is a complicated process. It's like cursing a spell, or summoning a rune: you're just smooshing magic together and hoping nothing bad happens. And, as the Wise Old Man says, 'hoping nothing bad happens is basically inviting the bad into your bedchambers'. We'd have worded it differently, but you get the idea.
