(Trivia) Prior to the removal of Lifeward, enchanted steel bolts could restore Lifeward.

(Journal) Sharpened rods of metal, enchanted with magic. A surefire way to guarantee that your enemies have a particularly bad time.

In Fellhollow these bolts were vital against the undead, as they provided that additional firepower needed to take down the relentless tide of shambling corpses.

name: Fang Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips carved from animal fangs.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 1x Small Animal Fang, 2x Ash Logs, 1x Feathers

description:
Fang arrows are power level 2 ammunition crafted at a Crafting Table.

(Journal) For a short time, a necromancer arrived on Ashenfall. She had found her way here by boat, fleeing pirates who wanted revenge for her misdeeds. Her skills were limited; she could not raise undead legions, but she had a knack for controlling simple fangs and bones. 

She fled into the forests – pirates having found Ashenfall and hunting her down – where she would unleash fang arrows against her foes in the hope of stopping their chase. It didn’t work. Broken, lost and without hope, she prepared herself for death. 

But death never came for her. 

Instead, a Wild Knight, who wore a mask made from the skull of a wolf, rescued her. He pushed back her assailants and brought her to safety. Their fellowship after that was unbreakable, though no bond of romance flowed between them. She made the arrows, he fired the bow, and together, they feasted on their victories and kept the woods safe from unwanted intrusion. 

Even now, there are signs of their friendship. Hidden across the forest, miniature carvings of a wolf skull and a bat can be found in places that meant something to them.

name: Fang Barbed Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips carved from animal fangs.

description:
Fang barbed arrows are fang arrows with weapon barbs crafted on the arrow. Like other barbed arrows, the icon will have a Bleed icon placed on the top right of the arrow to distinguish itself from regular arrows. There are no additional bonuses at this time. 
Note: fang barbed arrows are currently not craftable in either regular or Creative Mode worlds, making them unobtainable.

name: Fang Fire Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips carved from animal fangs.

description: Fang fire arrows are fang arrows with fire oil applied with level 45 Ranged. Targets that are hit by the fang fire arrow will not be inflicted with the Burning debuff, but higher-tier arrows will have a higher chance of doing so. Like other fire arrows, the icon will have a fire icon placed on the top right of the arrow to distinguish itself from regular arrows.

name: Goblin "Swingslash"

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A surprisingly nasty little axe. Popular with goblin warriors.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- CLUB COMBO attacks that deal SLASH DAMAGE, with increased DAMAGE

- Reduced DURABILITY

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 4 / 59 - 104 / 46 / Ascension Core (Power Level 4) 1; 5 / 76 - 135 / 52 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 95 - 168 / 59 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 115 - 204 / 66 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 135 - 240 / 72 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 156 - 276 / 79

description:
The goblin "Swingslash" is a power level 2 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a crafting table. The recipe is learned by consuming a cruel goblin blade, received as a random drop from a goblin pack; the drop chance for this vestige is 2%.
Despite having slash in the name, this weapon deals crush damage and uses the mace attack style. It has slightly higher base damage but the same durability as the bone club, despite listing a special effect of -15% durability.
It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores, but the base damage doesn't scale properly: the power level 2 goblin "swingslash" has 11-12% higher base damage than the power level 2 bone club's 26 - 46, but the power level 7 goblin "swingslash" only has ~1% higher base damage than the power level 7 adamant mace's 114 - 202).

(Journal) Contrary to popular belief, a goblin is as smart as any other species. It was Bandos that instilled within them the notion that intelligence was a sin, and demonstrating your education was something to be discouraged. As a result, goblins often go out of their way to make themselves seem less intelligent than they really are.

Hence "swingslash", the name given to this axe because of how it swings through the air, slashing anything it hits. It's so reductive and silly, it can only be an overcorrection, a desperate attempt by the creator to seem dumber than they are.

You can ignore, therefore the curve of the blade and the sharpness of the edge, created by carefully thought-out techniques that make the weapon deadlier than those before them. The name, chosen by the blacksmith, so none might accuse them of the crime of being smart.

name: Granite Maul

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: The power of this warhammer should not be taken for granite.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- BATTERING RAM
Deals heavy DAMAGE to the target and KNOCKS them DOWN

- OVERKILL
Uses a unique WARHAMMER COMBO that excels against SINGLE TARGETS

- UNWIELDY
Reduced ATTACK SPEED

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 1x Imbued Granite Maul Head, 1x Ornate Maul Handle, 1x Imbued Leather Wrappings, 8x Vault Shard, 1x Vault Core

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 4 / 97 - 140 / 46 / Ascension Core (Power Level 4) 1; 5 / 127 - 184 / 52 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 160 - 232 / 59 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 196 - 283 / 66 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 231 - 334 / 72 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 266 - 385 / 79

description:
The granite maul is a power level 3 two-handed melee weapon craftable after the quest Granite Mauled. It is classified as a masterwork weapon. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is that it hits harder but slower than other warhammers, and its special action is called Battering Ram, which will knock down most opponents. It has no effect on minibosses or bosses. Although it has a unique animation, other two-handed warhammers special actions also knock down most opponents.
Although this weapon has a different, very slightly slower attack style than other two-handed warhammers, it has a far higher damage range at every power level that makes it stand out when ascended: bronze warhammer (PL3, 52 - 82), iron warhammer (PL4, 76 - 119), steel warhammer (PL5, 100 - 157), mithril warhammer (PL6, 126 - 198), and adamant warhammer and tzhaar-ket-om (PL7, 156 - 244).

(Journal) While metal may be the preferred choice of weapon makers, the Granite Maul stands as a testament to the raw power of stone. This legendary weapon, revered among hammer wielders, is nothing more than a massive, heavy stone affixed to a stick. Yet, in the hands of a skilled wielder, it becomes a force of unparalleled destruction.

It was developed by ancient dwarves long ago, after one dwarf got fed up with the rock hammer he was using to fight a nest of gargoyles. The beasts were strong and numerous, and their skin was almost impenetrable to conventional weaponry; only rock hammers seemed to hurt them. In frustration, one dwarf took the biggest hunk of granite he could find and turned it into a legend.

Since that moment, the weapon has been refined, using various special components to make it more wieldy in combat. The original creator having[sic] done himself an injury with the recoil.

name: Grieving Moonstaff

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: This staff is dedicated to Lougrim, the fallen Garou goddess of the Moon.

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 4 / 3.9 / Ascension Core (Power Level 4) 1; 5 / 5.2 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 6.6 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 8.1 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 9.6 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1

description:
The grieving moonstaff is a power level 3 staff that can be crafted at a mystic forge. The recipe is unlocked after studying a mysterious crescent carving, which can be dropped by garou druids with a 2/100 drop chance. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is -15% critical strike chance, which alongside its lower rune damage modifier at every power level, makes this the weakest staff to ascend.
For example, compare this to the draconic staff: That staff has +15% critical strike chance but has -15% durability to compensate. However, it has the same rune damage modifier as most other staffs at the same power level, while this staff has less, with no benefit to offset the reduced chance to crit.

(Journal) Lougrim was a moon deity, born to a cold world of soft silvers and silence. Her people lived lives of quiet contemplation, each moment spent wondering about the next. They were passive, soft spoken and sedentary, which drive Lougrim wild.

When a doorway to another world appeared and a grieving god wandered through it, Lougrim took the opportunity to run. To flee to another place, and live a life that she could endure.

History skips the next bit. Her closest allies have never learned what elevated her from her previous form to that of the goddess of the hunt, but whatever it is was profound enough to change her completely. She no longer resembled her silent kindred. She was quiet, yes, but in the way a tiger is moments before the kill. She is contemplative, true, but it was the stillness of a spider waiting for its prey.

When she found the garou, she knew she found her real kindred. They were violent, and deadly, and they yearned for the hunt. When she took her place as their goddess, she focused and refined them, creating hunters that were capable of felling almost any prey.

Yet still she kept the moon as her symbol, a reminder of her home and how far she has come since leaving it.

Now her priests bear the symbol, atop their staves and as the focus on their altars. They accept and revere Kuldra as their High Queen, yet they grieve the moon goddess that made them who they are today.

name: Hunter Stagbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: With it's[sic] aerodynamic antlers, this bow is very popular with garou scouts.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 18x Antler, 6x Ram Horn, 4x Swamp Thread, 4x Jade, 4x Vault Shard

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 5 / 67 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 84 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 102 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 120 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 138

description:
The hunter stagbow is a power level 4 longbow that can be crafted at a fletching bench. The recipe is learned by consuming a string of sinew, a vestige dropped by garou hunters with a 3/100 drop chance. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is 10% increased draw speed, making this weapon draw faster than other longbows.
This weapon also has slightly higher base damage than other longbows, making this, in combination with the draw time reduction, the ideal longbow to ascend for players wishing to focus on pure damage, though Ulv's Longbow will still be better for the first shot due to its special effect.  
When repairing this bow, 3 Antlers are required at a Fletching workbench.

(Journal) Gahl was a garou druid who lost everyone he knew. In the wars inflicted on his people by the other races of Ashenfall, he grew jaded with the cruelty he saw all around him. This reached its peak when he found a garou village in ruins and goblins dancing and laughing as they threatened a newly born pup, in her crib.

The village is gone now, dragged beneath the soil. Gahl’s vengeance unleashed upon the goblins, erasing them from existence. He took the child as his own and raised her in a way alien to his people – he raised her with love.

She had no talent for magic, and could not learn his druid spells, so he taught her how to hunt with a bow, and she was a natural. Dahnu, as he named her, made a bow out of the first deer she and her father had hunted and that bow became a symbol to all she encountered.

In time she would claim a king’s seat. Defeating the prior monarch with reason and wit. Charming him out of his power and offering her people another way.  

Her people thrived, making her father proud.

Until Velgar brought her reign to an end.

name: Imaru's Talon

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A Scimitar forged from the Visage of Imaru.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- Soul Feast
GRANTS a portion of HEALTH when killing an ENEMY

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 1x Undead Draconic Visage, 1x Steel Scimitar, 12x Vault Shard, 1x Vault Core

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 6 / 63 - 133 / 59 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 77 - 162 / 66 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 90 - 190 / 72 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 104 - 219 / 79

description:
Imaru's talon is a power level 5 scimitar, crafted at a blacksmith's bench, after receiving the serrated claw as a drop from Imaru. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is Soul Feast, which grants 15 health when killing an enemy. This effect has a 30 second internal cooldown. The player's maximum health, enemy type, or power level does not change the amount of health restored.
This is the only ascendable scimitar, and it has higher damage ranges when the same power level as the steel scimitar (49 - 103), the mithril scimitar (62 - 130), and the adamant scimitar (76 - 160).

(Journal) The essence of an undead dragon, distilled down into a blade. What could go wrong?

This weapon is cold to the touch in ways far beyond chilling. Holding it feels as if you're out in the cold, with no shelter to protect you. Exposure in the palm of your hand.

Worse than the cold, is the hunger. This scimitar wants to cut, to stab, to slice and to maim. It wants to see your enemies bleed so that it can feast on their suffering. Imaru may be dead, but her hunter is eternal and you feel it infecting you with each swing of the blade.

Still, the power of this blade makes it almost worth it. What's a little hunger when faced with the destruction of your foes? Lament later, surely, and revel now in the carnage. Perhaps there's a little dragon in you too?

name: Iron Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips forged from iron.

description:
Iron arrows are power level 4 ammunition that can be crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) Iron Arrows are sturdy and sharp, capable of piercing most armour. Brynmoor soldiers regularly employed them in the war against the garou. 

Village blacksmiths toiled for weeks at a time, creating countless arrows to be slung into battle. They literally poured blood, sweat and tears into the cooling metal, each arrow containing a drop of their hatred of the beastmen. 

The arrows were effective, brutally so. The arrows forged by blacksmiths who had lost loved ones to the conflict seemed to hit harder still. Vengeance manifested in metal.

name: Iron Barbed Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Lacerating arrows with barbed tips forged from iron.

description:
Iron barbed arrows are iron arrows with weapon barbs crafted on the arrow. Targets that are hit by a iron barbed arrow will be inflicted with the Bleed debuff, damaging the enemy by 5% of their max health for six seconds. Like other barbed arrows, the icon will have a Bleed icon placed on the top right of the arrow to distinguish itself from regular arrows. There are no additional bonuses at this time.

(Journal) The first of these weapons was not commissioned for war. Nor was it commissioned for hunting. Instead, this most deadly arrow was created for nothing more than vengeance.

Against a pigeon.

Lord Gawurin was the ruler of Brynmoor, as appointed by the priests of Saradomin. He wore expensive garments of the finest materials, adorned with glittering jewels and gold chain. So, he was most affronted when a single pigeon determined that such a garment was the perfect restroom choice.

The pigeon's audacity was unforgivable. Day after day, Lord Gawurin's garments were defiled by this feathered fiend. His anger grew, fuelling a desire for revenge that consumed him. He commissioned an arrow, a weapon of brutal design, with a single purpose- to make the pigeon suffer.

With a sinister smile, he summoned the most skilled hunter, a woman who had brought down countless foes, and ordered her to end the pigeon's reign of terror.

She stood at the top of the castle, her bow steady, her aim true. The tension in the air was palpable as she prepared to unleash the arrow of vengeance upon the pigeon. The world seemed to hold its breath in anticipation.

She missed.

name: Iron Bolts
description:
Iron bolts are a power level 4 ammunition that can be fired from iron crossbows.

(Journal) One sad aspect of human nature is that it will always strive to craft deadlier and deadlier weapons. Iron crossbow bolts were harder than their bronze counterparts, capable of penetrating the toughest garou armour.

Obrimex, of the garou, once tried to replicate the weapons. He crafted little, sharpened tubes of iron that he felt would match their power. Alas, the garou hadn't crafted crossbow technology, and throwing these little metal darts largely proved to be irritating rather than dangerous.

name: Iron Crossbow

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Blightwood, 6x Swamp Thread, 1x Iron Crossbow Limbs, 1x Jade, 4x Vault Shard

description:
An iron crossbow is a power level 4 crossbow that can shoot blurite, iron, and bronze bolts. It is crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) Iron turned the war against the garou more than some people would like to admit. They would claim superior training, tactics, and skills of their soldiers, but the truth is far simpler. Iron was strong and iron weapons were brutal.

Ranged weapons proved effective against the garou leadership, bound as they were by strict codes of honour. A thane was a deadly opponent up close, but if you could pierce their internal organs before they were within a swing’s reach, then they were no more dangerous than any other beast. It is perhaps no surprise then, that there was a race to create weapons to challenge them.

The people of Brynmoor had learned of a Wild Knight invention, a weapon that would allow one to deliver powerful ranged attacks, whilst still allowing the bearer to wield a shield. They took this design, studied and refined it and then upgraded it to include the power of iron weapons.

Garou numbers dropped rapidly as a result, turning the war heavily against them. In their desperation, the garou turned to their goddess and she, in turn, sought allies with deadlier weapons still.

name: Iron Dagger

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A sharp, compact weapon, perfect for quick strikes in close combat.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 6x Iron Bar, 3x Ram Horn, Wool Thread, 4x Vault Shard

description:
The iron dagger is a power level 4 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a small dash forward, followed by an upward slash, and can be useful as a combo extension.

(Journal) Iron Daggers are dangerous weapons in skilled hands. Light, quick and sharp as can be, they cleave flesh from bone before the victim knows they’ve been assaulted. This is why they became a favourite weapon of the Children of Shadows.

Though the cult rarely harmed anyone — it was mostly a social club — there were those among their number who took their calling seriously.

They forged their own daggers and honoured their master by adding a single drop of their own blood as the blade cooled. Some carved demonic pacts into the metal, though it is not known whether this actually created a compact.

name: Iron Fire Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Burning arrows with tips forged from iron coated in fire oil.

description:
Iron fire arrows are iron arrows with fire oil applied with level 45 Ranged. Targets that are hit by the iron fire arrow will be inflicted with the Burning debuff, damaging the enemy by 5% of their max health for six seconds. Like other fire arrows, the icon will have a fire icon placed on the top right of the arrow to distinguish itself from regular arrows.

(Journal) Rasthin was the master of fire. It was the gift she had stolen from the “soul of the world” as she called it. She could use the inner flame to inspire confidence or rouse people into a great fervour. The fire could reveal secrets, forcing truth from those who stood before her. But, more practical than all of that was one simple truth, that fire could burn.

There were many a dragon that tried to battle Rasthin directly, believing their dragonfire could destroy her. Their bones litter Ashenfall. It was only Queen Kuldra herself who could challenge the dragonkin, and theirs was a battle that left scars in the lands for centuries.

These arrows borrow a piece of Rasthin’s power. Able to inspire only by the fear they kindle in the wielder’s enemies. Yet, kindle they do, for those who face these flames will surely feel echoes of the fury wrought by the dragonkin lord of fire.

name: Iron Greataxe

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A massive, two-handed axe, capable of delivering devastating blows.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Iron Bar, 6x Oak Logs, 4x Hard Leather, 4x Vault Shard

description:
The iron greataxe is a power level 4 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) Few sights are as intimidating as a Great Axe hefted toward you. It can only be carried in a pose that exudes raw strength. The bearer of such a weapon rarely looks meek.

Bandos was also a fan of the aesthetic. While he favoured the sheer brutality of the Kyzaj, he chose to wield a Great Axe against Velgar. He stormed Brakka’s Folly, Great Axe in hand, and challenged the dragon to single combat. A god versus a dragon, the outcome felt obvious. Yet it did not play out as Bandos expected.

It should have been easy. Yet Velgar’s stone-touched flesh turned away Bandos' blows, and his poisonous breath leeched Bandos’ strength. Bandos cut a great scar down Velgar’s side, yet it was not, and the counterattack sent Bandos reeling.

He never surrendered, but there was no victory for the big high war god. He sounded a tactical retreat, seeking a better strategy – far, far away.

name: Iron Greatsword

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A well-balanced, large, imposing sword for skilled warriors.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 10x Iron Bar, 4x Hard Leather, 2x Wool Thread, 4x Vault Shard

description:
The iron greatsword is a power level 4 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at the blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a large circular slash that lunges the player forward in the direction they are aiming, useful for hitting large groups simultaneously and changing directions during a combo.

(Journal) The Iron Greatsword is a devastating weapon favoured by the most powerful warriors. The strongest garou warriors wielded them in battle against goblin invaders, turning armies of green-skinned soldiers into nothing but viscera.

When the dragons turned on their allies, the Greatsword was likewise turned on armoured scales. Several dragons underestimated the power of such a weapon in the hands of a skilled wielder. Garou thanes tore young dragons to pieces, wearing their bones in victory.

This made them clear targets for older dragons. Velgar, a mighty general, marked those wearing dragon bones for death. He crushed them first, brutally and swiftly. Their strength shattered beneath his claws or swallowed in an instant.

The practice of wearing bones quickly fell out of favour.

name: Iron Mace

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Crush your foes with this heavy, spiked iron mace.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 8x Iron Bar, 8x Oak Logs, 4x Hard Leather, 4x Vault Shard

description:
The iron mace is a power level 4 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a small leap with an overhead slam, dealing moderate damage.

(Journal) Few instruments are as good at shattering bones as the Iron Mace. It was a favourite weapon of White Knight paladins, who dreamed of shattering the bones of the risen dead. Necromancy was rare on Ashenfall, though not unheard of. Two necromancers had been reported to the order: a girl with a knack for bones; and one who whispered to the dead. Neither summoned skeletal hordes for the knights to shatter.

But garou and goblin bones broke just as well. In the war against the garou, Sir Lear, a White Knight paladin, used the mace to great effect. He crushed warriors, battered druids and shattered the shields of powerful thanes. He was a symbol of the might of Saradomin's faithful in the face of overwhelming odds.

He joined the Wild Knight commander, Vemmeck, in their siege against a northern garou stronghold. With countless goblins at their side, their victory was almost assured. Yet a single druid's magic held the forces at bay, until Sir Lear learned how ineffective his mace was against the scales of a dragon.

name: Iron Sword

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A well-crafted iron blade for skilled combatants.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 8x Iron Bar, 4x Hard Leather, Wool Thread, 4x Vault Shard

description:
The iron sword is a power level 4 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a forward stab, which can reach quite far forward compared to most melee attacks, making it useful for combo extensions and intercepting an opponent before they can attack.

(Journal) It was iron that nearly brought about the end of the garou. Swords forged of the metal were death in handheld form.

The blacksmiths of Brynmoor churned out countless numbers of Iron Swords, depleting the village's iron supplies. Each soldier was equipped with such a weapon and each warrior was ready to cut through the horde.

The garou are strong, dangerous and deadly. Their weapons are powerful, and their strikes fierce. Even the magic of their druids puts the Wizard's Guild to shame. Yet their armour fails to turn away iron's wrath. As humans advanced, iron weapons in hand, they razed villages to the ground and wiped out whole families.

Lougrim wept for the loss of her children, and her cries changed the course of the war.

Iron is strong, but it melts at great temperatures, and there are no flames as strong as a dragon's breath. As Lougrim bound herself to the service of the Cabal, all that was left of the villagers were puddles of molten metal.

name: Iron Warhammer

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A brutal two-handed weapon, capable of smashing through enemy defences.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Iron Bar, 2x Hard Leather, 4x Vault Shard

description:
The iron warhammer is a power level 4 two-handed melee weapon crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a slow and heavy slam in front of the player, with a small area-of-effect shockwave that will cause a hard knockdown on most opponents and deal heavy damage.

(Journal) Imcando dwarves preferred the forge to the battlefield but were not afraid to join the frontlines when their aid was needed. They waded into conflict with warhammers held high, ready to smash their enemies out of existence.

Only one Imcando dwarf made her way to Ashenfall, and she came here for vengeance. Her foes were not the garou or the dragon army, but the green-skinned goblins who had earned her ire.

She was given a wide berth in Bramblemead, partially because of the enormous hammer hefted across her shoulder but mostly because of the fury that radiated, as if her hate were flames and she was perpetually burning. In the rare times the dwarf spoke, she simply mentioned that she was looking for someone the goblins had taken, and she would never rest until she got them back.

name: Keris

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: This dagger is thin and has a wavy edge to better slide through gaps in armour.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 8x Adamant Bar, 6x Dragon Tooth, 3x Desert Thread, 2x Gypsum Wax

description:
The keris is a power level 7 dagger. The recipe is learned from the corroded curved blade, found in the vault in southwest Umbral Sands, in the chest after the kalphite queen boss fight. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect deals 25% increased damage against kalphites, including kalphite workers, kalphite soldiers, kalphite guardians, and the kalphite queen, but not to kalphite eggs. While upright, kalphites are resistant to all forms of damage other than fire, however, when knocked onto their backs either with enough damage or after a parry, they become weak to all forms of damage, increasing all other forms of damage by about a combined 85% (this weapon's first hit deals 50 damage to an upright kalphite and 92 damage when knocked down without a parry, while the adamant dagger deals 40 damage upright and 74 knocked down without a parry).
This weapon and the adamant dagger have slightly higher maximum hits compared to the dragonbone dagger and wolfbane dagger when ascended to power level 7 (59 - 150 vs. 59 - 152), however they excel in their respective areas: In Umbral Sands, the player can be ambushed by kalphites at any time, and the kalphite guardians and kalphite queen can become immune to one of the three combat styles, so carrying this weapon out on the sands even when geared for either Magic or Ranged (especially since it only weighs 5.0) is worthwhile. Similarly, dire wolves, dragonwolves, ghost wolves, and hellhounds will quickly close the gap, so the wolfbane dagger is a strong choice against them. In all other situations, the dragonbone dagger's increased crit chance (even though it will be a lower bonus against those specific enemy types) will be best in all other situations.

(Journal) The Moon Garou believe this weapon was given to them by a goddess of the river, who took the desperate garou and raised them up to become masters of the desert sands. The weapon was created as a tool against one of the deadliest denizens of the dunes – the kalphites.

The blade tip can find its way through the chinks in the Kalphite exoskeleton, piercing through the chitinous armour and damaging the much squishier flesh beneath. It was turned many a battle against the Kalphites from a garou bloodbath, to a garou victory banquet – though they tend to find the Kalphite meat a little less appetising then they’d like.

Moon Garou champions are gifted the Keris dagger after achieving a great victory. It is a symbol of their bravery and marks them as skilled warriors to all the other tribes. In olden times, a bearer of the Keris would be treated with great respect. They would be given food, lodging and anything else they needed to further their victories.

Nowadays, however, the Keris is seen more as a tool of survival against the insectoid foe.

name: Kuldra's Wrath

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A masterfully crafted wand, infused with the fury of Kuldra - channeling arcane power with terrifying efficiency.

description:
Kuldra's Wrath is a power level 9 wand and opening the Queenslayer's Reward Pack. Unlike many other weapons in the game, this wand is both uncraftable and has a passive full durability.
Bug: Despite the special effect stating an increase to damage against dragons, this wand does not currently get a damage boost against dragons.

(Journal) When Kuldra was no bigger than a terrorbird, the dragonkin Viika would play with her. They had bonded - the dragon and the seer. It is hard to imagine that this was the same Kuldra whose five heads would eventually loom over Ashenfall.

Their early relationship had but one frosty moment. Viika's eyes glazed over and they grabbed a stick and thrust it into Kuldra's paw. Kuldra screamed and tried to rip the stick out, but it was a splinter that her teeth couldn't reach. It had retreated too far into her body. The playmates were pulled apart, with Viika screaming fragmented nonsense about "bringing a weapon to the world" and "I did what must be done, yet also did not".

Kuldra was confused about the sudden betrayal. She retreated into the pile of rags that she had made into a nest. Later, Viika approached Kuldra with an upturned palm, their thoughts more lucid. They asked Kuldra for forgiveness, and Kuldra gave it happily.

But while they returned to being friends, Kuldra was unable to remove the splinter. It itched and ached as it pushed further into her bloodstream.

name: Magic Longbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: The natural resilience of magic wood allows this bow to send arrows soaring over great distances.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Magic Logs, 3x Rune Bar, 6x Vis Fibres, 3x Dragonstone, 3x Draconic Vis Wax

description:
Magic Longbow is a power level 8 longbow.

(Journal) The garou spoke in hushed tones about a hunter in the eastern reaches of the Fractured Plains. They knew well enough not to approach her: she would keep to hunting game, unless the garou posed a threat. If a young garou was unwise enough to rush her, she would punch an arrow through their throat.

The hunter wouldn't hide herself particularly. While she was hooded, her weapon of choice was a magic longbow, and it would surge with energy like a lightning bolt in the Highlands. The hunter knew that she could not be touched; that the garou could watch her all they wanted.

All the garou could do was share stories about her. Trackers said that she moved without leaving a trail - something that meant she was neither human or goblin. Others claimed that they heard soft music in her territory and promptly forgot why they were there. One garou even claimed to see a shadow of the hunter - a version completely in black.

name: Magic Shortbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A shortbow made of magic wood, this bow is light enough to carry all day and powerful enough to ruin someone else's.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 7x Magic Logs, 2x Rune Bar, 3x Vis Fibres, 2x Dragonstone, 1x Draconic Vis Wax

description:
Magic Shortbow is a power level 8 ranged weapon.

(Journal) A warning for a very particularly kind of ranger: magic wood has a tendency to twinkle. Now, if you're the creed to hide in the shadows, then you might want to reconsider the magic shortbow. It is phenomenally accurate and a delight to use, but it doesn't half draw attention.

Of course, you can embrace the problem. I remembers stories about The Glittering Assassin in Varrock. The last thing you would see before dying is something fabulous in your peripheral vision.

name: Maple Battlestaff

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A magical weapon carved from maple wood.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 16x Maple Logs, 6x Mithril Bar, 3x Glass Vessel, 16x Infernal Fragment

description:
Maple battlestaff is a power level 6 two-handed staff that can be crafted with a mystic forge.

(Journal) The Children of Shadows were never a grateful sort, but they would acknowledge that the groves of maple in Dowdun Reach were a boon. Almost everything wooden in the keep - from the library bookcases to the bannisters - was made from maple.

Alric relished walking among the maple trees. For so much of his life, he had been encased in stone and surrounded by essence: working long hours in the keep. But the maples were for thinking.

In his twilight years, Alric carried a maple staff with him: the Subjugation Staff. It was a crutch for an old man, yes, but it was also a way to bring the grove with him. When he couldn't muster the energy to visit his favoured trees, he carried a remnant with him.

infobox.label: Description

description:
The maple longbow is a power level 6 longbow that can be crafted from a fletching bench.

(Journal) A supple wood, is the maple. When cut into long, reed-like lengths, it can be formed into a worthy longbow. The process also releases syrup - a treat for a day's fletching. Not enough to make a maple toastie, mind, but enough to leave a sweet taste in the mouth.

Bramblemead was often the venue for archery competitions, and the maple longbows would be out in force. Etched into the trophy, you would find many Rasmodels. They were a noble bloodline on Ashenfall, and would often add to their reputation by earning combat trophies.

description:
Maple shortbows are a power level 6 bow that has higher stats than the willow shortbow. Players can create the maple shortbow at a fletching bench.

(Journal) Putrilius, the cthonian demon, will tell you that any living thing can be possessed. If needs must, a cthonian can be a cockroach or spider, for a time.

In one desperate moment, after the Dreaming Stone was shattered, Putrilius was forced to possess a maple tree. It wasn't an experience she enjoyed. Most curiously, she found themselves aligning to the maple's inner cadence. Everything slowed. Putrilius barely registered a thought in two years.

What woke Putrilius was a logging axe. Their maple body was toppled and then fletched into an armature. For a moment, as Putrilius's life faded from the wood, she was a shortbow.

It was the closest she had come to dying. With a cognitive spark, she moved from the bow to a passing hound before all her lifeforce ebbed away.

name: Maple Wand

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A finely crafted maple wand, prized for its natural affinity with magic.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 8x Maple Logs, 3x Mithril Bar, 2x Glass Vessel, 8x Infernal Fragment

description:
The Maple wand is a power level 6 magic weapon. It can be crafted at a mystic forge using 8 maple logs, 3 mithril bar, 2 glass vessel, and 8 infernal fragment.

(Journal) The Brynmoor School of Magic fell to fire, and it didn't rally in another location. The school, it was said, had been losing money, and the wizards saw the fire as an opportunity to count their insurance money and cut any further losses. The students were left to apprentice elsewhere, if they could find the work, or practice their magic in other, ill-thought-out manners.

Upon the death of a foremost wizard, an old dean of the School of Magic, a chest was wheeled out. Inside were hundreds of sticks, wrapped in cloth. The wizard's family believed them to be incense sticks or diffusers - scented with holly berries, as per a decoration on the stick's base. The family sold them for a single gold piece each. A poster was attached to the front of the chest with the words 'Fire Sale - Incense Sticks' .

It is hard to describe the carnage that followed. The sticks were not incense but splitbark and maple wands, and those wands were intensely powerful. They were infused not with the smell of holly berries, but with the elements of fire, water, air and earth. When lit, they reacted explosively, and when held, they fired chaotically. Brynmoor was alight that night, and everyone had a different story of what happened to them, from stoves encased in rock to clothes blown clean off by air magic.

Most of the wands were discarded or destroyed. But a few found their way into the hands of commoners - those who were not allowed, or could not afford, to practice magic. Street urchins, scullery maids, chimney sweeps. Each of them had the beginnings of magic in their hands.

name: Master Wand

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A wand worthy of an accomplished spellcaster. Mastery is not included.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 8x Yew Logs, 3x Refined Obsidian, 2x Infinity Cloth, 2x Dragonstone, 2x Gypsum Wax

description:
The Master wand is a power level 7 magic weapon. It can be crafted at a mystic forge using 8 yew logs, 3 refined obsidian, 2 infinity cloth, 2 dragonstone, and 2 gypsum wax.

(Journal) Holly Arnuld was buried with a Master Wand on her chest and her hand clasping it. Her last wishes, found in her desk, made it clear that the wand was to be placed as close to her heart as possible. A few other preparations were to be made, like the timing of the funeral, and her closest companions made them.

As Holly was lowered into the ground at her funeral, her friends, fellow teachers and class raised their wands to the sky. It was respectful and somber, as was Brynmoor tradition.

Just as the congregation was looking to disperse, the coffin shook, and the seams around the lid brightened. The coffin blew open and a flurry of fire spells exploded from the Master Wand. A nearby tree was set alight. Students had to use their jackets to stamp out fires on the lawn. Everyone claimed to hear cackling from the coffin, yet - when a brave teacher stooped over to have a look - Holly was still in repose, blackened a little with soot.

It turned out that Holly was buried with a magical mechanism on her chest, timed to trigger at the end of the funeral. The cackling was the whirring and sputtering of the mechanism. The machine acted as a catalyst for the wand, and - well - you know the rest.

name: Master's Staff

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A magical staff fashioned for a master of the mystic arts. It radiates with power.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 16x Yew Logs, 6x Refined Obsidian, 4x Infinity Cloth, 4x Dragonstone, 4x Gypsum Wax

description:
Master's staff is a power level 7 two-handed staff that can be crafted at a mystic forge.

(Journal) Before the master wand, there was a staff of such power that the mages of the wizard’s tower decided it was too dangerous to keep. They placed the staff in teleportation circle, scrambled the coordinates and hurled it through the Abyss to settle far away from Misthalin.

In truth, it should have ended in the depths of the sea, sinking down and down into the darkness, but something caught it instead.

A powerful elven mage had found their way to Ashenfall, and they had already indulged in powers darker than what their kin traditionally allowed. They felt the staff hurtling through the Abyss and used their unnatural sorcery to pull it to them, so that they might benefit from its power.

This elf and his retinue found their way to the Umbral Sands, where they challenged one of the Moon Garou’s mages to a magical duel, over some perceived slight or other. The battle was magnificent, power that shook the dunes and cast a great sandstorm into the skies. The garou was defeated, but not before her spells shattered the master’s staff.

In his arrogance he cast the remains aside and continued his journey into Ashenfall. Moon Garou would find the remnants of the staff and found a way to recreate it. Weaker than the original, true, but still possessing a power that would make lesser mages tremble.

name: Mithril Barbed Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Lacerating arrows with barbed tips forged from mithril.

description:
Mithril barbed arrows are a power level 6 ammunition that are crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) Demons dealt with wounds and ailments on their own. There was no such thing as a demon surgeon or sick bay. If wounds were fatal then the demon would die; if wounds were survivable, then survive they did.

This was an observation of Summoner Flament, who passed it on to Alric, who idly mentioned it to Lord Rasmodel in one of their weekly meetings. As with most information, Lord Rasmodel examined it for opportunities.

If demons sought no help from their wounds - no remedies, no medical assistance - then his knights would carry weapons that took advantage of that fact. Arrows were poisoned, since no demon carried antipoison. And arrows were barbed, as demons would pull them roughly from their hides, rather than remove them carefully.

It was a small advantage, but Lord Rasmodel took it. As he would often say, "stack opportunities, one on top of the other, and soon you will have an impregnable tower".

description:
A mithril crossbow is a power level 6 crossbow that can shoot mithril, steel, blurite, iron, and bronze bolts. It is crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) A mithril crossbow is the standard issue for any modern Black Knight. If you showed capability, then you might be promoted to Black Knight Sniper, and that came with the Black Sniper Crossbow. But for the average Black Knight, the crossbow was a long-kept friend.

The crossbow's main purpose was to stop demons in their tracks. The Zamorakian magi claimed to keep their demon hordes under control, but demons tested that claim.

The crossbow had other uses. Remove the bolt, rest the crossbow on the floor stock-upwards, and you had a stool. Sit on the floor and it was a headrest.

You could also waste time shooting ravens. Shooting the red, glowing ravens was an immediate dismissal, however. Alric demanded they were protected, for reasons that he never expanded on.

The mithril dagger is a power level 6 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) Doric likes to remind Vannaka that you wouldn't find a dwarf making daggers.

As Doric says, "it's a very human thing, a dagger. A dwarf never hides their weapon: we're polite enough to show what you're up against. An' you won't find us attacking from the back or sides. No sir, we bonk you from the front."

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Burning arrows with tips forged from mithril, coated in fire oil.

description:
Mithril fire arrows are a power level 6 ammunition that are crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) The Fogger's Gala was one of the few dates that a Black Knight could look forward to. An annual tradition, it would take place on the mistiest day of the year. As soon as low clouds started rolling in, word spread among the knights that it was Gala day.

It was an informal event on the battlements of the keep. There were quivers that represented each of the night's events, and the knights would name their arrows and place them into the quivers of those they wanted to participate in. Arrows were drawn randomly to determine the order.

Sergeant Blister was on hand with betting. He brought his blackboard, which he seemed to have on-hand when needed, and a week's wages were placed on friends and adversaries.

The events all revolved around bows and crossbows. The fog made it almost impossible to see anything, so the Gala was a test of both memory and accuracy. One event required the archer to hit hay bales with fire arrows. The hay bales were invisible, so they only had location names to go by - the hut by the waterfall, Skrexis's bed - which meant firing Hail Mary's in the vague direction of their quarry, hoping that it would ignite in the night.

Other events included Pin the Arrow on the Goblin (as you can probably imagine, a noisy goblin ran about in the fog), Farthest Arrow and Alric's Curtains.

description:
The mithril greataxe is a power level 6 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) In the early years of Dowdun Reach, the concept of a mithril greataxe would have been unthinkable. A big, showy weapon that used large quantities of mithril would have been seen as a betrayal. The Children of Shadows, holding a monopoly on mithril, wanted to present it as a rare metal. At best, the richest on Ashenfall might have a brooch or tiara that sparkled with mithril.

Nowadays, Doric can have two greataxes whipped up for you before dinner. Much has changed.

name: Mithril Greatsword

infobox.label: Description

description:
The mithril greatsword is a power level 6 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) "You see a mithril greatsword, I see a mithril dagger," Vannaka would say. He would then pick two up from Doric's forge, one in each hand, and try not to register effort. It was a routine, a little play, between Vannaka and Doric.

This time, however, the joke was on Vannaka. Doric had made his mam's rock cakes, and folded some mithril round them - one for each hilt.

Vannaka wobbled. "Cripes," he said.

description:
The mithril mace is a power level 6 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) The standard term is mace, but Vannaka prefers bludgeon. "It's one of those sound words, like stomp and grunt, right? When I hit someone with it, it bludges. Bludge, bludge, bludge."

"You're thinking of onomatopoeia," Dionysius said, helpfully. "Nah, but good try. I'm thinking of breakfast," said Vannaka.

description:
The mithril scimitar is a power level 6 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) The scimitar form is not commonplace on Ashenfall. Unlike the mainland (where you can't walk five metres in the Kharidian Desert without getting slashed by one), the scimitar is a rarity. Only an offshoot of the Garou, found in some of the harshest deserts of Ashenfall, are known to wield it.

That is likely to change, of course, as more adventurers make landfall. It makes you wonder what the island will look like in five, ten years' time as the cultures intertwine.

description:
The mithril sword is a power level 6 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) Mithril may not be the strongest metal on Gielinor, but it's perhaps the most begulling. It's metal that benefits most from looking at it up close. Each sword has unique imperfections.

It's a quality that makes it the most popular choice for ceremonial swords. Go back in time and watch a knighting ceremony in Dowdun Reach, or bestowal of honours in Bramblemead. You will see your share of mithril swords.

description:
The mithril warhammer is a power level 6 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) The mithril warhammer was once the weapon most associated with Lord Rasmodel of Dowdun Reach. He was rarely seen without it. In the mornings, when he was most in pain, it would be a prop, something to lean on while the night's watch recounted the events of the early hours. In the afternoons, it was a beautiful warning, a threat of what might happen if you disobeyed him.

Lord Rasmodel wasn't one for naming his weapons. He found the custom a little juvenile. But when his thoughts were elsewhere, you might see him pat the head of the warhammer. There was kinship there, even if he wouldn't admit it.

name: Necromancer's Staff

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Necromantic essence still emanates from this staff.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 24x Undead Bone, 6x Sacred Oil, 4x Fine Thread, 6x Vault Shard

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 6 / 7.3 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 8.8 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 10.3 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 11.8

description:
The necromancer's staff is a power level 5 staff that can be crafted at a mystic forge. The recipe can be obtained by entering a spectral door and interacting with a dragonkin effigy in Vekchenven Kara, the dragonkin vault in central Fellhollow. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is the highest rune damage modifier of all staves at the same power level but with lower durability.
It's only higher than the staff of light by 0.1. At power level 7, this equates to only a 0 - 4 damage difference between the two depending on the rune type, hit of the combo, whether it crits, and whether a magic focus is used. This will only make a difference if that damage hits a breakpoint on certain enemies (i.e. if it takes one less hit with this weapon to defeat an enemy than with the staff of light). The staff of light has 20% more durability with 1300. Although managing durability with Magical Mending is trivial, it could make a difference in, say, the 30 waves of the fight caves.

(Journal) Necromancy isn’t inherently evil, despite what some of the scriptures might say. Whilst some cruelly force the dead into service, others make bargains and pacts with spirits, offering them a chance to influence the mortal world again, rather than simply watch events unfold.

In Fellhollow a small group of mages encountered a smoking fissure in the earth. From it they heard strange whispering voices in the darkness, promising them power and knowledge. Greedily they listened, making pacts with the whispering in exchange for the ability to bind the dead to their service.

In life they performed their arts in secret, raising corpses none would miss, or binding ghosts no one even knew were haunting them. Yet in death, that’s where their true power lay.

With their souls withered away and consumed by the dread Imaru, the necromancers were no longer limited by the last vestiges of morality, and with the new powers at their command, turned a struggling defence against the undead, into a horror-filled nightmare where each fallen ally would rise as a foe.

name: Oak Battlestaff

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A magical weapon carved from oak wood.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Oak Logs, 6x Anima-Infused Bark, 3x Wool Thread

description:
Oak battlestaff is a power level 3 two-handed staff that can be crafted with a mystic forge.

(Journal) Saradominist mages preferred the hefty swing of the Oak Staff over the more pliable ash. They felt that sturdier oak allowed for more powerful spells. The more durable wood was less prone to shattering itself into splinters when they cast their most devastating magic.

While most wizards practised familiar spells, pushing their research into different practical applications of what was already known, one wizard would push the boundaries of spellcasting itself. Her name was Cynthia Valtis, and she would go down in local legend.

She would have liked to be remembered for her ability to transform twigs into carrots, thus preventing the famine that threatened Brynmoor. She would have wanted to be remembered for her clever application of wind and water magic for creating a nice cool breeze during the summer heat. But, alas, she would be remembered for an ill-advised fire magic experiment that sent her travelling across the continent faster than any wizard before.

Her body has yet to be found.

name: Oak Longbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A powerful longbow carved from oak wood.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Oak Logs, 6x Wool Thread, 2x Bronze Bar, 2x Opal

description:
The oak longbow is a power level 3 bow that can be crafted at the fletching bench.

(Journal) The Longbow is every hunter’s friend. Capable of taking down prey over a greater range than the Shortbow, it has been the end of many a deer trying to flee through the woods. 

Bramblemead would host a thrilling archery tournament. The villagers would proudly bring their own Longbows, meticulously crafted by hand, and compete to take down cleverly hidden targets scattered across the village. It was a spectacle of skill and precision, with the only rule being that the target must be shootable from the open street. 

With the introduction of magic, the competition took on a whole new level of silliness. Participants conjured magical air currents that sent arrows astray – often into unsuspecting washing lines or pies cooling on windowsills – or they would playfully blast arrows out of the air with fire spells. 

However, this stopped after the Amalgamated archer, Derien, joined the game. Gifted with the element of air, his arrows curved gracefully with each shot, missing traps, tricks and deceptions. His victory earned the Amalgamated more jealousy, which led to the competition ending out of envious spite.

name: Oak Shortbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: An agile shortbow carved from oak wood.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 8x Oak Logs, 3x Wool Thread, Bronze Bar, Opal

description:
The oak shortbow is a power level 2 shortbow that can be crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) The villagers who proved their skills with an ash shortbow were brought into the forest by a Wild Knight instructor in search of more durable wood. The oak stood proud and tall in the forest, standing firm against the ebb of time. Villagers would gather the sturdiest branches that they found and bring them to a quiet place in the woods to begin carving their new bows. 

The Wild Knight would tell them that a good bow is more than just a weapon; it is an extension of oneself. They encouraged each villager to put a piece of themselves into the bow, a decoration on the handle or a poem carved into the wood. Whatever made the bow personal to them. 

This connection in the crafting process would help the villagers feel comfortable with their new weapon, and many young hunters would use the same bow throughout their lives. It even became a tradition for young hunters to gift a bow to their beloved as a marriage proposal. A tradition that survived into the Third Age.

name: Oak Wand

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A sturdy oak wand that offers reliability far beyond its humble appearance.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 6x Oak Logs, 3x Anima-Infused Bark, 2x Wool Thread

description:
The Oak wand is a power level 3 magic weapon. It can be crafted at a mystic forge using 6 oak logs, 3 anima-infused bark, and 2 wool thread.

(Journal) There was a room in the Brynmoor School of Magic that every new student visited at least once. The students' purposes differed, of course: some students wanted to see if it was merely myth; others wanted to simply observe it; a few wanted to go a little further...

The room was Arnuld's Sanctum. In the centre of the circular room was a single pedestal with an oak wand. From a distance, it looked like it floated, but step closer and it would be clear that it was supported with a stand of glass. There were no inscriptions on the pedestal, no decorations on the walls. The room lacked any detailing, outside of a single sprig of holly, etched onto the lower-half of the wand.

No one had been able to grasp the oak wand to take it. Any fool who tried would be overcome by the sensation that they were on fire. They would drop to the floor, contorting in an effort to remove flames that were not there. Only the stupid and self-worthy would attempt it, and there was always a crowd of third- and fourth-years to watch and laugh at them.

When the School of Magic fell to fire (which had nothing to do with the wand), no one had the presence of mind to visit the Sanctum. Fire surged up the pedestal, and the wand's magical protection dropped. Embracing the fire, the wand was consumed, as if it were finally with its own kind. Then the pedestal dropped and something opened.

name: Pharaoh's Sceptre

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: This ancient and powerful weapon lets the wielder channel its sovereign authority into mind-controlling powers.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- SWORN SERVANT
Summon a FRIENDLY KALPHITE to ATTACK and distract enemies in combat.
Resummoning while your summon is still active will RE-SUMMON it with the SAME HEALTH as when dispelled.

- ROYAL MANDATE
Cast Confuse without consuming RUNES while wielding the PHARAOH'S SCEPTRE

- HOLLOW VESSEL
While a SUMMON is ACTIVE, you regain STAMINA slower than normal.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 10x Gold Bar, 10x Scorch Leather, 32x Shimmerscale Powder, 4x Dragonstone, 4x Gypsum Wax

description:
The pharaoh's sceptre is a power level 7 staff that can be crafted at a mystic forge. The recipe is learned from the Icthlarian fetish, the reward from the quest Contact!. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is Royal Mandate: While holding the Sceptre, the wielder is able to use the Confuse spell without consuming runes. Its special action is Sworn Servant: This summons Buddy, a friendly kalphite to attack and distract enemies in combat. Buddy can be used for up to 3 minutes as long as it is still alive, and will take another five minutes for it to respawn when recasting the sceptre's special action. However, due to Hollow Vessel, while Buddy is active, the wielder regains stamina 10% slower than normal.

Bug: There is currently a bug where Buddy will not respawn, or spawn in a online world.

(Journal) The Moon Garou tried the whole Pharaoh concept exactly once. Unused to non-violent systems of government, they gathered together as a people and pulled stones from a bag to decide who was the luckiest of all of them, and therefore who deserved to rule.

It was, as you can imagine, not a smart system of governance.

The winner was a garou called Hakanaten, and he did not want the job. He had always been an outsider, far more interested with the goings on of the nearby Kalphite hives then he was with the goings on of the city. Still, he had been chosen by an assumption of destiny and was set upon a throne with crown and sceptre in hand.

He hated it. He made decisions as best he could, but could never please everyone. If he tried to help one person, it angered another. If he cast judgement on a lawbreaker, he was deemed cruel by some and weak by others. No matter what he tried, he only found himself more and more isolated from his kin.

In the end a revolt saw him deposed and the throne destroyed. He was cast into the hive he so adored, where he was expected not to live for long. Yet, he had studied the hive and he could mimic their behaviours better than some of his own people’s. He helped them dig tunnels. He joined them on hunts. He lived a life far happier among the hive then he ever did at home.

The sceptre, that had been cast down with him, carries with it a measure of his fondness for the insects. It is said that anyone who wields it, can call on the hive for aid, in memory of an unlucky monarch.

name: Poisoned Adamant Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips forged from adamant, coated in Weapon Poison.

description:
Poisoned adamant arrows are a power level 7 ammunition that are crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) While adamant arrows might be considered deadly enough, there are still those that would push it further. The Moon Garou hunters found that if they dipped their arrows in deadly snake venom, then their enemies would fall faster and with less danger to the hunting party.

Unsavoury bandit types found them useful as well, for far less practical a purpose. When they would raid caravans, they would strike the guards, drivers and occupants, with poisoned arrows, so that even if their victims could escape across the dunes, they would not live long enough to warn other caravans of their fate.

name: Poisoned Bronze Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips forged from bronze coated in Weapon Poison.

description:
Poisoned bronze arrows are bronze arrows that are coated with weapon poison. Targets that are hit by a poisoned bronze arrow will be inflicted with the Poison debuff, damaging the enemy by 5% of their max health for six seconds. Like other poisoned arrows, the icon will have a Poison icon placed on the top right of the arrow to distinguish itself from regular arrows.

(Journal) The Wild Knights were not above poison, any edge in a battle was worth having. Poison meant that you could take down a dangerous beast, even if your initial shot wasn’t a mortal one.

The druids among the order felt little concern over its use either, after all nature is filled with wielders of poison and so the Wild Knight archers were simply emulating nature’s tools.

name: Poisoned Fang Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips carved from animal fangs coated in weapon poison.

description:
Poisoned fang arrows are fang arrows that are coated with weapon poison. Targets that are hit by a poisoned fang arrow will be inflicted with the Poison debuff, damaging the enemy by 5% of their max health for six seconds. Like other poisoned arrows, the icon will have a Poison icon placed on the top right of the arrow to distinguish itself from regular arrows.

(Journal) The Children of Shadows loved using these. The very notion of bone and poison combined as a weapon; it touched some deep dark part of themselves and filled them with a malicious sort of glee.

Alas such weapons proved relatively useless in any secret campaigns against the Saradominists of Bramblemead. Certainly, they could assassinate a baker if they needed to, but against a knight it would just ping harmlessly off their armour.

Still, they made for good talking points at the secretive meetings, making enjoyably sinister table-decorations that paired well with the wine and cheeses.

name: Poisoned Iron Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips forged from iron coated in Weapon Poison.

description:
Poisoned iron arrows are iron arrows that are coated with weapon poison. Targets that are hit by a poisoned iron arrow will be inflicted with the Poison debuff, damaging the enemy by 5% of their max health for six seconds. Like other poisoned arrows, the icon will have a Poison icon placed on the top right of the arrow to distinguish itself from regular arrows.

(Journal) Lougrim abhorred the use of poison on arrows, she felt it cheapened the hunt. The mages could wield it in their spells, but a hunter should produce smooth, quick kills, creating as little suffering as possible.

Most garou, in turn, would at first refuse to use poisons on their arrows. They followed her teachings, and they hunted swiftly and cleanly. After Lougrim’s fall it became clear just how foolish it was to seek such a merciful path, their new High Queen had made it clear that they should use all tools at their disposal.

name: Poisoned Mithril Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips forged from mithril, coated in Weapon Poison.

description:
Poisoned mithril arrows are a power level 6 ammunition that are crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) The Rasmodels were notorious for their use of poison. When they lived to the south, in Temple Woods and Bramblemead, it was often said that you should cover your cup, mouth and ears around a Rasmodel. One of the family was finally caught red-handed (or green-handed, considering the poison used), and the rumour moved to certainty. They were banished to Dowdun.

The reputation followed them, and mostly became a gift rather than curse. No-one in Dowdun Reach wanted to cross the Rasmodels for fear of waking up in spasms.

We say that it was 'mostly' a gift, because of an event between a young Lord Rasmodel and his cousin. Lord Rasmodel claimed that he could shoot an apple from the top of his cousin's head, and promptly did so. He handed one of the resulting apple-halves to his cousin who ate it, and promptly keeled over and died.

It turned out that the arrow used to the cleave the apple was poisoned. Lord Rasmodel claimed that he had been using his father's hunting arrows, and one of them must have been tainted. It seemed entirely plausible.

But there was still doubt. And that doubt grew into a reputation: a reputation that outmatched his own family's. Even at the age of eight, the inhabitants of Dowdun Reach gave Lord Rasmodel a wide berth.

name: Rune Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Rune arrows are prized for their exceptional flight and striking power.

description:
Rune arrows are a power level 8 ammunition that are crafted at a fletching bench, and can be used to craft rune barbed arrow, poisoned rune arrow, and rune fire arrow, though players may wish to simply use Adamant Arrow as they possess the same base damage.

(Journal) You might think that rune is the last metal you would use for an arrow. Rune is a magical metal, and it has diamagnetic properties (meaning that it repels other metals, sometimes with force). You don't want to be aiming at a garou berserker, only to watch the arrow arc away from them.

As Vannaka would say, 'your problem is that you're thinking like an amateur'. Archers don't actually WANT arrows to hit other metals: they want to slip into the gaps between armour, puncturing an armpit or neck. The best archers also love a trick-shot, hitting an opponent through a sea of allies. The trick is to use the diamagnetism to your benefit, and that - again, to quote Vannaka - 'comes from the hardest skill of all. Practice'.

description:
The Rune Bolts are a power level 8 ammunition crafted at a Fletching Bench. Despite being power level 8, these bolts deal the same damage as adamant bolts.

(Journal) You may have wondered where the phrase 'out of the blue' or 'a bolt from the blue' comes from. Its origins are actually from Misthalin, from the humans who made their way through the mountains to Isafdar. Elves are a stealthy bunch, so the first thing a human soldier might know about the ambush would be an arc of blue (the 'blue' being the rune metal). The soldiers would worry about being shot by 'a bolt from the blue', which is where the saying originated.

Also see 'the thin blue line' and 'screaming blue murder'.

name: Rune Crossbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A precision-engineered rune crossbow that delivers powerful, accurate shots at range.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Magic Logs, 4x Vis Fibres, 1x Rune Crossbow Limbs, 1x Dragonstone, 1x Draconic Vis Wax

description:
A rune crossbow is a power level 8 crossbow crafted with a fletching bench.

(Journal) Guard duty in Kuldra's Tower was a thankless task. Few could or would approach the tower, as inaccessible as it was. But the shifts were called and there was always a small group of crossbow-wielders posted to the entrance to the tower, waiting for the unlikely approach of an enemy.

But while it was boring, you still had to be on your toes. Kuldra's Tower was prone to crumble and breaking, particularly at the entrance where the guards were posted. Well-prepared guards would make their own grapple-bolts, coiled and ready by their feet. If their seat started to spiral away into the anima ether, they would socket the grapple-bolt and hope that their shot was good enough to find purchase in the rock. If not, well, they would find out what it feels like to anima-shift at a fatal rate.

name: Rune Dagger

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A razor-sharp rune dagger prized for its speed, precision, and deadly effectiveness.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 5x Rune Bar, 4x Harmonised Compound, 2x Vis Fibres, 1x Draconic Vis Wax

description:
The Rune Dagger is a power level 8 one-handed melee weapon.

(Journal) Kuldra's generals were prone to a spot of gallows humour. In the evenings, over a drink or two, they would argue about Kuldra's heads and which of them they would prefer to be killed by. Their tone would only be half-joking. They had all been in the presence of Kuldra when she was displeased, and saw the looks of those who had displeased her. They knew (from the expressions of the damned) which head caused the slowest, most painful death.

The poison head was the one they wished to avoid. They carried a rune dagger in their boots, in the event that they fell foul of it. It was better to die by one's own hand than perish by Kuldra's poison.

name: Rune Fire Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips forged from runite coated in fire oil.

description:
Rune fire arrows are a power level 8 ammunition that can be crafted with a fletching bench.

(Journal) The rune fire arrow is central to a story about the knight commander, Sir Leigh. In his will, Sir Leigh requested a full-boat burning. He wanted to be pushed out to sea, towards the mainland where he was born, and an archer was to set the pyre alight with a rune fire arrow. Sat at his desk, writing the will, it would have sounded like a fantastic idea to Sir Leigh. But in reality it was very different.

Rune, you see, has repulsive properties. It is diamagnetic. So when Sir Leigh was laid to rest in his gold armour atop a raft, and the archer tried to aim for the pyre-wood beneath him, the rune arrows would not hit. Dozens upon dozens of arrows were fired, and they all deviated from their path thanks to the runic properties. By the time a boat was sent out with a man holding a lit torch, two seagulls and one shark had been set alight.
