name: Rune Greataxe

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: An imposing rune greataxe, for when a regular axe simply isn't sending a strong enough message.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Rune Bar, 3x Magic Logs, 4x Black Dragon Leather, 2x Draconic Vis Wax

description:
The rune greataxe is a power level 8 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted with a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) It may surprise, but there was once a Garou King in Kuldra's Tower. Kuldra, perhaps fearful of a mutiny (or having to kill everyone who mutinied, diminishing her forces), allowed the various troops to keep their customs. That included the Rite of the Moon, where garou would challenge each other for the privilege of becoming the King. Her initial belief was that, if the garou were content on challenging each other rather than her, then it would be the best for all involved.

That ended with King Rí Túath. Rí Túath had delusions of something beyond grandeur. He claimed to have been visited by Lougrim, who had crawled out of Kuldra's gullet while she was sleeping. According to Rí Túath, Lougrim was a prisoner in the belly of Kuldra, and it was the job of the Garou to recover her. He led a contingent of garou against a sleeping Kuldra, and carved into her skin with a rune greataxe.

In a sense, King Rí Túath achieved his aim. He made it inside Kuldra, and did, in fact, find Lougrim. It didn't happen in the way that he might have wanted, and he certainly wasn't alive for any of those steps.

Kuldra was quick to deny the garou the Rite of the Moon after King Rí Túath.

name: Rune Greatsword

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A massive two-handed blade forged from runite. Few can wield such a weapon effectively, but fewer still can stand against it.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 8x Rune Bar, 3x Black Dragon Leather, 2x Vis Fibres, 2x Draconic Vis Wax

description:
The rune greatswordis a power level 8 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted with a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) Kuldra's army is such a disparate mix of creeds and motivations that it's a miracle that everyone hasn't ended up killing each other. I mean, some friendly fire certainly happens, but the fear of Kuldra almost always wins in the end. If there is going to be any collateral damage, Kuldra would prefer that it comes from her.

She made an example once, to show her position. A garou thane, fondly known as The Muggathug, had a habit of slaying the black dragons. She would leap into the black dragon nests, lop off a head with her rune greatsword and then boil the head in a kitchen pot. The resulting skull would be painted in garou tribal colours and then nestled on her head. Muggathug liked having a different helmet for every day of the week.

Kuldra felt that The Muggathug was encroaching on her territory. She commanded that The Muggathug attended her, before she bit off The Muggathug's head, boiled it in a mixture of ice and fire, and tasked her smiths with making a ring for her. Muggathug's skull became the centrepiece of a solitaire ring that Kuldra wore on those days where she needed to be a little dressier.

name: Rune Mace

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A sturdy rune mace, designed to crush armour and bone alike with devastating force.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 5x Rune Bar, 6x Magic Logs, 3x Black Dragon Leather, 1x Draconic Vis Wax

description:
The Rune Mace is a power level 8 one-handed melee weapon.

(Journal) It's not hard to see why a place in Kuldra's army was tempting for a goblin. Back in Brynmoor or Ghornfell, the diet was dirty water and rats. Your armour would be stolen from the weakest goblin you could find, and your weapon was likely to be a femur bone (with any luck, not your own) or a bronze sword that was more rust than bronze.

In Kuldra's army, it was entirely possible to be promoted to wield rune armour or weapons (Kuldra was at least wise enough to know that goblins shouldn't be given sharp weapons, so most of the time they would wield a mace). Goblins became, well, liabilities. They were used to whacking each other and doing barely any damage at all. It was culturally engrained to boff each other on the head as a kind of wake up call. But a rune mace would make that wake up call rather messy, and a playful thwack would lead to arms flying off.

name: Rune Scimitar

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: The curved rune blade flows effortlessly from one strike to the next.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 6x Rune Bar, 3x Black Dragon Leather, 1x Vis Cloth, 1x Draconic Vis Wax

description:
The rune scimitar is a power level 8 one-handed melee weapon that is crafted with a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) Kuldra always liked the crescent shape of the scimitar. It reminded her of the moon goddess, in pieces within her belly. The curved scimitar shape recalled her claws.

As a result, the scimitar became the weapon of her most trusted warriors. They were her Talons - extensions of herself. Whenever a task required a swifter, more delicate touch, she would employ them. Her army would learn to fear being gutted by the Talons, almost as much as being gutted by Kuldra herself.

name: Rune Sword

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A finely balanced rune sword, renowned for its strength, precision, and reliability in battle.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 6x Rune Bar, 3x Black Dragon Leather, 2x Vis Fibres, 1x Draconic Vis Wax

description:
The rune sword is a power level 8 one-handed melee weapon.

(Journal) Runite is not readily available to everyone in Kuldra's army. Kuldra preferred that it - alongside magic wood - was reserved to the upper reaches of her army.

It is easy to look at her chaos of heads and think that she somehow represents disorder, but Kuldra instilled hierarchy in her troops. You needed to earn your place at the top of her troops, and she was consistent in what earned that place. You had to be inconspicuous enough to never draw her attention, and you needed to avoid anyone who might draw that attention. Suffer fools, and you suffer with them. Stand within metres of them, and you suffer even more dearly.

name: Rune Warhammer

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A colossal rune warhammer, capable of shattering shields and crushing the strongest defences.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Rune Bar, 2x Black Dragon Leather, 2x Draconic Vis Wax

description:
The rune warhammer is a power level 8 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted with a blacksmith's bench.

(Journal) Nothing pleased Kuldra more than The Battering. Her armies were handed warhammers and greataxes, and they each found a corner of the tower. Kuldra would wait in her chamber and then signal the start of The Battering, firing a beam of moonlight upwards into the sky.

Her troops would slam their weapons into the stone of the tower, sending reverberations throughout. She placed her claws onto the stone, and would feel it shake. She knew when a wall would separate or floor break apart; she could sense the tower weaken through her scales. It delighted her to feel the work of the Kin diminishing, scattering to the anima winds. But most of all, she relished the sensations. Her strength was such that she could rarely feel anything anymore, yet the shockwaves registered, however dimly. It was one of the few moments in her late life where she could feel anything at all.

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A crossbow made from black metal. Similar to those used by Black Knight snipers.

- Slower FIRE RATE

description:
The shadow crossbow is a power level 6 crossbow that can be crafted at a fletching bench. The recipe is unlocked after studying the sinister mechanism, which can be found in chests throughout Dowdun Reach or purchased from Postie Pete's Evil Emporium for 300 infernal fragments. It can be ascended at a mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect deals 15% increased damage to weakpoints, however it has +25% Reload Duration, meaning it reloads slower than other crossbows.
When looking to maximize the damage done per metal or enchanted bolts, this is the pick. However, as it reloads slower than most other crossbows and the blurite crossbow and dorgeshuun crossbow reload faster than most other crossbows, it reloads significantly slower by comparison. One of the most useful aspects of a crossbow is the flinch that they cause per hit, and those are simply able to do that more often. The choice comes down to what bolt type is preferred, as the dorgeshuun can only fire bone bolts.

(Journal) Climb the turrets of Dowdun Reach in its prime, and you would have found the Black Knight Snipers. These were the elite marksmen of the Black Knights, tasked with looking outward when the rest of the order would look inward. They would scan the skyline for threat - for the beating wings of a dragon. There was no greater trophy for the Black Snipers.

One[sic] one occasion, a bolt was loosed at Imaru. She had arrived at the keep for diplomatic purposes, and was rewarded with a bolt to the neck. You could see the conflict within her, as her urges were swallowed. For a second, a disdainful eye moved to the Black Sniper. But she reset and continued to talk to Lord Rasmodel and Alric like nothing happened.

Restraint was certainly beaten into the Black Snipers that night.

description:
The shadow sword is a power level 5 greatsword created using a blacksmith's bench. The recipe is learned by consuming the shard of smoky glass, dropped from a zogre. It is required to complete Doric's Quest to receive the zombie axe. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is +25% damage against spectral enemies such as lost souls, ghost wolves, and soulstone sentinels.
It has almost exactly the same stats as other greatswords with Titan's Wrath as the one exception, and although it can be valuable in Fellhollow, extra damage to spectral enemies is useless outside of that region. Still, the zombie axe is the best one-handed crush weapon available to ascend, especially as it also deals slash damage, so getting this weapon just for that is worthwhile.

(Journal) It might be better to refer to this sword as a smoke sword, given its wispy nature, but there is no denying that this is an ephemeral blade aligned with the world of the dead.

It feels cold to the touch and sometimes, when you least expect it, you are almost certain you can hear whispering coming from the blade.

name: Skullsplitter

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A deadly weapon with a disturbingly accurate name.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- Increased CHANCE of landing CRITICAL HITS with CLUB ATTACKS

- Reduced BLOCK

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 6x Bronze Bar, 4x Antler, 4x Oak Logs, 2x Hard Leather

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 4 / 56 - 99 / 46 / Ascension Core (Power Level 4) 1; 5 / 73 - 130 / 52 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 92 - 164 / 59 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 113 - 200 / 66 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 133 - 236 / 72 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 153 - 272 / 79

description:
Skullsplitter is a power level 3 one-handed weapon that can be crafted using a blacksmith's bench. The recipe is learned by consuming the vestige remnants of a shattered skull, received randomly as a drop from killing garou berserkers at a 1/50 drop rate. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores. 
Its special effect is +15% critical strike chance, which equates to an average 1.0375x damage increase. However, that assumes that the critical strike chance never goes over 100%, which would be wasted. Currently, the base chance is 10%, the 2/3 melee armour set bonus provides 50% after a block, and the lesser Attack potion provides 25%, equaling 85% before adding the Skullsplitter's 15%.
This weapon has slightly higher base damage than the goblin "Swingslash" but slightly lower than the zombie axe at equivalent power levels. The zombie axe, however, deals both crush and slash damage, making it worse against enemies weak to crush but resistant to slash (including skeletal hoplites, zogres, black knight warriors, black knight guardians, and the black knight titan). For those enemies specifically, this is the best one-handed crush weapon to ascend.

(Journal) Garou children would often play pretend at great, epic battles. They would create their own stories, true, but they enjoyed reenacting the battle of legend, and no character was more popular than King Raluh, the mighty.

Pups would wander into the forests in search of the sturdiest stick they could find and then announce to the other children that they were the king, and this stick that most legendary of weapons - Skullsplitter.

As the legends go, King Raluh had been granted a weapon by the Moon Goddess, Lougrim. A weapon capable of destroying any foe. Armour was as paper to Skullsplitter and fables had him crush the bones of villain and monster alike.

It is, therefore, no surprise that as the garou pups mature, they create weapons to match the legends, and garou warriors wield mighty maces carrying that mythical name. Though the true Skullsplitter may just be a story, these powerful imitations are no less deadly.

name: Splitbark Staff

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A Mage's Weapon crafted from wither-rotted hollow bark. It has strange magical properties.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 16x Hollow Bark, 6x Sacred Oil, 4x Fine Thread, 6x Vault Shard

description:
Splitbark staff is a power level 5 two-handed staff that can be crafted with a mystic forge. Players can unlock this after receiving hollow bark in their inventory for the first time.

(Trivia) The appearance of the item closely resembles that of RuneScape's (RS3) Splitbark wand.

(Journal) Magic always inspires people. Something about rewriting the underpinning rules of your reality, with little more than force of will and a handful of stones, makes people reach for lofty goals. In Fellhollow it was the wizard Falistrius who wanted to make a name for herself.

She wanted to be a magical scholar. A researcher who might uncover the secrets of the universe itself. They sought spells of greater and greater power, dabbling in mysteries both profane and forbidden, and came up empty-handed.

After constantly searching for power, it was an unexpected duel that would grant her the fame she sought, at a price she would have preferred to avoid. A travelling elven sorcerer arrived in the village of Emberwood one night and the local drunk foolishly picked a fight with him. Unfortunately for Falistrius that drunk was her wife.

The elf challenged the drunk to a duel, for satisfaction over a drink spilled, and by local custom Falistrius was forced to answer. They met in the forests of Fellhollow, and unleashed their magic.

The elf’s spells were like nothing she had ever seen before. Cold and dark, sanguine and terrible, they tore into her magical defences like they were nothing and writhed inside her soul like a foul nightmare. Against the strain, her staff shattered, leaving her vulnerable. In desperation she grasped a fallen hollow tree branch and urged her magic through it.

It wasn’t enough to save her. But it was enough to earn the respect and satisfaction of the sorcerer, who left the region with his pale-skinned cohorts. Ever since then, young Fellhollow mages would craft staves from the hollow bark from the forest, in memory of Falistrius.

name: Splitbark Wand

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Crafted from enchanted splitbark, balancing resilience with arcane potential.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 6x Hollow Bark, 3x Sacred Oil, 2x Fine Thread, 3x Vault Shard

description:
The Splitbark wand is a power level 5 magic weapon. It can be crafted at a mystic forge using 6 hollow bark, 3 sacred oil, 2 fine thread, and 3 vault shard.

(Journal) Brynmoor's School of Magic was little more than scattered rubble. There is very little as flammable as a wizards' school, thick as it is with books, potions and staves.

Rescue parties saved who and what they could, but seven casualties were tallied. They were mostly wizards whose luck had run out, who were practicing spells that left them incapacitated. They were in the midst of astral projection or alterations of the mind when the fire swept through.

Under the rubble, however, the rescue parties found something unusual. There was a room that wasn't on any plans, located beneath Arnuld's Sanctum. It wasn't particularly large: only a handful of wizards could have stood upright within it. But in that room was a plaque, lacquered to protect it from fire. On it was written "You have passed my trial. I have underestimated my fellow wizards. Take what is earned - Holly Arnuld".

On the walls, around the plaque, was row upon row of wands. Splitbark and maple wands in their hundreds.

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A mystical weapon humming with power, wielded by mighty Saradominist Wizards ages past.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 16x Blightwood, 8x Wild Anima, 4x Sapphire, 12x Vault Shard, Vault Core

description:
The staff of light is a power level 4 masterwork staff that can be crafted at a mystic forge. The recipe can be obtained by completing the quest Highlighting the Problem. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is a higher rune damage modifier than most other staves at the same power level.
It's only lower than the necromancer's staff by 0.1. At power level 7, this equates to only a 0 - 4 damage difference between the two depending on the rune type, hit of the combo, whether it crits, and whether a magic focus is used. This will only make a difference if that damage hits a breakpoint on certain enemies (i.e. if it takes one less hit with the necromancer's staff to defeat an enemy than with this weapon). The necromancer's staff also has 20% lower durability with only 1050. Although managing durability with Magical Mending is trivial, it could make a difference in, say, the 30 waves of the fight caves.

(Trivia) There was an unused status effect in the cache where the player would receive a 33% melee resistance for six seconds whilst wielding the staff, but it is not currently active in the game.
The staff gives off a small amount of light when wielded by the player in a dark area.

(Journal) In the Third Age, before someone could wield a Staff of light, it would first need to be blessed by three people.

A priest would bless it first, instilling the weapon with Saradomin's wisdom. A monk would bless it second, imbuing the staff with the humility of Saradomin. Finally, an icyene general would give their blessing, dedicating the weapon to Saradomin's righteousness.

Those battlemages chosen to wield such a sacred weapon would dive into battle against Zamorak's forces, and believed themselves invulnerable.

They were often proved wrong.

Yet, those who carried the staff into battle seemed to survive longer than their compatriots. The defensive magic of the staff kept them alive longer than others. A demon once stole a staff and tried to use that power for himself. Still, when he tried to channel demonic power through the staff, it is said that the explosion could be seen from across the battlefield.

description:
Steel arrows are a power level 5 ammunition that are crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) Traditional wisdom says that to kill a zombie, you must destroy the brain. This is disappointingly untrue in Fellhollow, the animating force of Imaru’s hunger needs no thought to drive it forward.

No, a far better plan is to destroy the bones and muscles with sharp metal-tipped spikes launched at the creatures with as much force as you can manage. Steel arrows perform this task very nicely.

name: Steel Bolts
description:
Steel bolts are a power level 5 ammunition crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) Sharpened bolts of steel projected at great speed is a formula for your target to have a very bad day.

Although it was cheaper and quicker to forgo the coal and craft iron bolts, the relentless nature of the undead hordes required a more practical approach. Steel was stronger than iron, and was more likely to put the ravenous undead back in the dirt where they belonged, making it very popular in the last few years of Fellhollow’s resistance.

name: Steel Crossbow

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 16x Willow Logs, 6x Fine Thread, 1x Steel Crossbow Limbs, 2x Jade, 6x Vault Shard

description:
A steel crossbow is a power level 5 crossbow that can shoot steel, blurite, iron, and bronze bolts. It is crafted at a fletching bench.

(Journal) There were no garou in Fellhollow for the people to deal with, so in the early days of the settlement people created steel crossbows primarily for hunting game. The dragons that guarded the people were gentle creatures, but possessed of an enormity so great that they required a great deal of food to keep going. Hunting, therefore, became a very popular activity, with many competitions and events crafted to provide meals for the draconic caretakers.
When the withering began to spread and the dead began to rise, steel bolts proved just as effective at piercing a zombie’s skull, as it[sic] would catching[sic] the quarry from a hunt. 

Though the dead would come in droves, the crossbow would let them be taken out at great distance, keeping the last remaining settlements safter[sic] for just a few days longer. Every moment counted in those final days.

description:
The steel dagger is a power level 5 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a small dash forward, followed by an upward slash, and can be useful as a combo extension.

(Journal) The Children of Shadows were very fond of steel daggers. They were powerful, dangerous and very expensive at the time, making them the perfect ritual tool to demonstrate their adoration of the god of chaos.

Mostly the offspring of wealthy families, the rituals of the Children were performed out of boredom more than religious fervour. They would gather at secret meetings and proudly display their elaborately carved daggers, trying to prove to each other who was the most devoted to the lord of darkness by way of expensive kitchenware.

If you asked any of them to use such a blade in battle, they would be more inclined to slit their own throats in fear, rather than mutilate their opponents.

(Journal) Some people just want to watch the world burn! Some people want to watch the world burn, but have thought through the logistics of fire and so decided to set the world aflame from a distance. These arrows are popular among the latter category.

name: Steel Greataxe

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A two handed Battleaxe forged from Steel.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 16x Steel Bar, 6x Draconic Leather, 5x Willow Logs, 6x Vault Shard

description:
The steel greataxe is a power level 5 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a large circular slash that lunges the player forward in the direction they are aiming, useful for hitting large groups simultaneously and changing directions during a combo.

(Journal) Power corrupts, and what's more powerful than an enormous axe comprised of metal stronger than any seen before? Such was the logic of Olga Skulltaker (not her real name), the self-styled bandit queen of Fellhollow.

As a child, Olga had always enjoyed listening to her grandfather's stories from the mainland. Tales of mighty warriors defeating terrifying foes. Purehearted heroes challenging evil knights to great battles across pointlessly high bridges and the like. Her parents always laughed and called her "their little hero" but the truth was she was far more interested in the villain.

When she was old enough to wield a weapon, she trained with the biggest axes she could carry, and her sparing partners feared facing off against her because she always took things too far. Once, this even cost another student their fingers.

As an adult, she found herself among the Children of Shadows. She had hoped they would be dangerous, wicked people, like herself, but instead they spent their time reciting terrible poetry and talking about evil, without ever doing it.

So she took her axe, changed her name, and found the highest bridge she could, and attacked anyone that tried to cross it.

name: Steel Greatsword

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A two handed Steel sword made famous by Highland Warriors.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Steel Bar, 5x Draconic Leather, 4x Fine Thread, 6x Vault Shard

description:
The steel greatsword is a power level 5 two-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a large circular slash that lunges the player forward in the direction they are aiming, useful for hitting large groups simultaneously and changing directions during a combo.

(Journal) It was the followers of Armadyl who enjoyed the greatsword so much, in defiance of the bows that were the more traditional choice. They said it reminded them of the legend of the godsword and would lament not knowing the secrets of forging one, as it would be quite useful against the Godeater, Kuldra and her call for humanity's death.

Sadly for the villagers, the art of godsword creation was never revealed, so they turned to steel instead. While significantly less flashy, and almost certainly not going to terrify any deities, a steel sword will do significant damage to anything not divinely attuned.

name: Steel Mace

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A brutal crush weapon forged from high quality Steel.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 8x Steel Bar, 4x Draconic Leather, 8x Willow Logs, 6x Vault Shard

description:
The steel mace is a power level 5 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a small leap with an overhead slam, dealing moderate damage and guard breaking quicker than other one-handed special attacks.

(Journal) The priests of Emberwood village were not as militant as their fellows back in Brynmoor. They saw little need for weapons, when a dragon watched over their flock. Still, they carried steel maces by their side to symbolize their office, each one ornately engraved with the symbol of their chosen deity.

Although the Saradominist priests had first insisted that different faiths could only turn on one another, they found an odd sort of kinship in their fellows, and would regularly enjoy debates on the merits and flaws of each other's faiths.

name: Steel Scimitar

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A vicious, curved sword of Eastern origins forged from Steel.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 10x Steel Bar, 5x Draconic Leather, 2x Fine Cloth, 6x Vault Shard

description:
The steel scimitar is a power level 5 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a small leap with an overhead slam, dealing moderate damage and guard breaking quicker than other special attacks. Despite being a sword-class weapon, the steel scimitar shares the special attack of mace weapons and the attack speed of the abyssal whip, while sporting its own unique attack animations.

(Journal) It is said that the origins of the scimitar come from Al Kharid, where skilled swordsmen would wield them in a dazzling manner akin to a dance. Travelling dignitaries would be wowed by the spectacle, applauding great choreographed sword clashes that dramatized legendary battles of past history.

They were brought to Ashenfall by a noble family during the god wars, who had taken up the scimitar as their weapon of choice, in service, of course, of the mighty Saradomin. This family was proud and pious, which made them all the more concerned when their daughter was one of the first to show the signs of Amalgamation.

Love, for once, triumphed over prejudice, and the family scorned their wealth and prestige in order to protect their child. They joined many others who fled the growing unrest in the village of Bramblemead and travelled north to Fellhollow. There, they taught the secrets of the scimitar to the local blacksmiths, and the weapon garnered a great deal of popularity in the times to come.

name: Steel Sword

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: For fighting monsters and swearing oaths.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 10x Steel Bar, 5x Draconic Leather, 3x Fine Thread, 6x Vault Shard

description:
The steel sword is a power level 5 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a forward stab, which can reach quite far forward compared to most melee attacks, making it useful for combo extensions and intercepting an opponent before they can attack.

(Journal) Atilius Rasmodel was a proud and powerful knight. Her skill with the sword was without compare and her bravery seemingly infinite against the dangers in Fellhollow. She was chosen by Imaru as one of her guards, not that a dragon needed such a thing, and she was responsible for the defense of the dragons when they fell into the weeks-long torpors they were known to suffer.

She called herself the Dragon Knight. Even though such a title was unofficial and self-proclaimed, it soon stuck among the village people and they would bow and nod in appreciation of her skill as they passed her.

When Kuldra descended on the region, demanding humanity's destruction, Atilius climbed on the back of Xikotal's back, hoping to drive her steel blade through the Godeater's heart. She died beside the dragon she had sworn to protect, free of all remorse, in the line of duty.

name: Steel Warhammer

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A massive weapon made from Steel. Great for hammering really big nails.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 16x Steel Bar, 3x Draconic Leather, 6x Vault Shard

description:
The steel sword is a power level 5 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. Its special attack is a slow and heavy slam in front of the player, with a small area-of-effect shockwave that will cause a hard knockdown on most opponents and deal heavy damage.

(Journal) Lionel wasn't good at much in life, but he could swing a hammer, and he could swing it hard. As one of the Amalgamated, born with hair of metal and skin of stone, Lionel worried that he would be hated as the Almalgamated in Brynmoor had been, but Fellhollow proved to be a kinder place.

Instead of being feared and shunned, his unnatural strength became a source of pride among his family and friends. Locals would challenge him to heft heavier and heavier things, cheering and lavishing him with praise as he did so.

Life had been good. He was happy. So, of course, it all had to end.

When the dead began to rise, arrows and blades seemed less effective than before, but crushing faces still got the job done. His family and friends escaped to the Silverthorn Keep and Lionel waited at the guardhouse, standing as a wall against the tide of the undead. Countless zombies and skeletons fell to his hammer, reduced to little more than powder in a few careful swings. He could have stemmed the tide if that were all, but when the zogre descended upon him, even Lionel's warhammer eventually broke against the strain.

name: Stone Arrow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Arrows with tips of splintered stone.

description:
Stone arrows are power level 1 ammunition crafted at a Crafting Table.

(Journal) The Stone Arrow's weight and durability make it a more popular choice among hunters. The hardness of the tip makes it better at piercing tough animal hides or less durable forms of armour. In the Second Age, druids considered it a form of cheating, citing that it required a human's ingenuity to create rather than being a gift of nature.

They seldom complained when the evening meal was served, celebrating the success of the hunt alongside everyone else.

Even with somewhere as remote as Ashenfall, some humans turned to banditry, and they were very fond of Stone Arrows. Cheap and easy to produce, they help to kill and threaten anyone who makes the mistake of travelling through bandit-controlled woodland.

One such bandit, the self-described 'bandit king, Otho', would choose only "interesting" stones to turn into arrows. Glittering pebbles that swished through the air. He was nicknamed the "Magpie King" because of his love for shiny pebbles. A moniker he was very unhappy with.

name: Stone Club

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A primitive weapon made from stone, perfect for early adventurers.

description:
The stone club is a power level 1 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a crafting table. This weapon is the first weapon a player learns to make at the start of their adventure. Its special attack is a small leap with an overhead slam, dealing moderate damage.

(Journal) A big stone attached to a stick; not terribly durable, but surprisingly handy. This simple weapon has saved the lives of many warriors. When caught between a rock and a hard place, why not take advantage of the rock?

Goblin children play a game called bonk-bonk-bash, a rather unpleasant little pastime that acts as a form of population control. Each of the goblins takes a rock, attaches it to a stick and then takes it in turns to thwack their friends with it. This is a traditional household game that keeps the costs of feeding the family low.

name: Stone Dagger

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A rudimentary blade, handy in close combat.

description:
The stone dagger is a power level one-handed weapon that can be crafted at a crafting table. Its special attack is a small dash forward, followed by an upward slash, and can be useful as a combo extension.

(Trivia) The black stone dagger mentioned in the journal is a reference to the black stones, materials associated to an eldritch entity known as Xau-Tak.

(Journal) One of the first weapons ever created, the Stone Dagger has a sinister history. At first, it allowed early humans, dwarves, elves and other intelligent species to thrive. They could take down prey and feast on the spoils, using the dagger to pare down the kill, making it easier to eat. It created the gap between animals and people, the first step toward civilization. 

It’s also the first tool to lead to murder. 

A young man whose name has long been forgotten once created a dagger of glittering black stone. Pleased with his work, he displayed it proudly, earning the admiration and envy from those around him. 

So proud was he of the dagger that he would whisper to it, acting as though it would whisper back. On the day he slit the chieftain’s throat, he claimed that the dagger had told him to do it. 

Fortunately, most Stone Daggers are pleasingly silent.

name: Subjugation Staff

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A powerful battlestaff, once owned and used by Arcmage Alric.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 16x Maple Logs, 6x Mithril Bar, 4x Glass Vessel, 18x Infernal Fragment

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 7 / 8.3 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 9.8 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 11.3

description:
The subjugation staff is a power level 6 staff that can be crafted with a mystic forge. The recipe is unlocked after studying the demonic metal rod vestige, which can be found in chests throughout Dowdun Reach or purchased from Postie Pete's Evil Emporium for 300 infernal fragments. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is 15% increased damage against lesser demons and abyssal demons. Despite also being considered demons, hellrats and hellhounds do not take extra damage from this weapon.
This weapon has the same rune damage multiplier as the draconic staff when ascended to the same power level, but it has much higher durability. That being said, with how few enemies there are that take extra damage from this weapon, the same thing applies here as for the draconic staff that the staff of light and necromancer's staff are better choices in most other situations as they will have 0.4 - 0.5 higher rune damage multipliers at each power level, and the increased chance to crit or higher durability aren't enough to offset that.

(Journal) Anyone who worked with Alric knew about the Subjugation Staff. It would thud, thud, thud on the cobblestone floor as he approached. It was a welcome warning that Alric was arriving, but it came with notes of dread.

The power of the Subjugation Staff came from what was rolled up and inserted into its middle. It was a demon pact, but one that had been defaulted on. A demon, not a human, had failed to keep their side of the bargain, and that gave the contract a radiating power. Alric captured that power within the staff. While he held it, it was as if all of demonkind owed him something.

name: Thane's Authority

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A hefting greataxe, wielded by the powerful garou thanes.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 10x Iron Bar, 8x Bronze Bar, 4x Oak Logs, 4x Vault Shard

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 5 / 113 - 197 / 52 / Ascension Core (Power Level 5) 1; 6 / 141 - 246 / 59 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 170 - 298 / 66 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 200 - 350 / 72 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 230 - 403 / 79

description:
Thane's authority is a power level 4 two-handed melee weapon created using a blacksmith's bench. The recipe is learned by consuming a brutal bladehead, received randomly as a drop from killing garou thanes and the Garou King, at a 1/20 drop chance. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is +15% stamina cost, but it only has around +5% base damage compared to the other greataxes at lower power levels and a mere +1% base damage compared to the adamant greataxe at power level 7.
The black greataxe has the same increased stamina cost, but has higher damage ranges at both power level 6 and 7 (146 - 256 vs. 141 - 246 and 176 - 308 vs. 170 - 298).

(Journal) Might makes right. This is the truth of the garou philosophy. Strength and cunning dominates all. The Garou thanes demonstrate this might in the weapons they wield. Though heavier and more tiring, this axe swings with deadly force, capable of cleaving through almost any armour.

The design is passed down to the garou from templates granted to the first garou blacksmiths by divine revelation. Lougrim taught them about the curve of the blade, and the heft of the hilt. Designed for the hunt, it could fell most quarry in a single blow.

Under Kuldra’s leadership, the chosen quarry was human. The dragon queen had a deep hatred for the humans, she found them weak, petty and flawed. The Thanes carried out her orders, using the axe to wield their authority, in her name.

name: Titan's Wrath

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: This sword is now thrice-owned: by you, the Black Knight Titan and Lord Rasmodel.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- FLAMES OF RAGE
Trigger FIRE EFFECT around you, dealing DAMAGE to all enemies and triggering BURNING on them

- BURNING EXECUTION
KILLING an enemy with the SPECIAL ATTACK ENCHANTS the sword with FIRE. Killing an enemy REFRESHES the ENCHANTMENT effect

- ENCHANTED WEAPON
You cannot cast additional ENCHANTMENTS on this weapon

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Black Metal Bar, 5x Blue Dragon Leather, 4x Mystic Cloth, 64x Infernal Fragment, 1x Broken Titan's Wrath

infobox.label: Item Sources
infobox.value: Black Knight's Fortress Reward Pack (Qty 1, Always)

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 7 / 132 - 229 / 66 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 155 - 268 / 72 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 177 - 307 / 79

description:
Titan’s wrath is a power level 6 greatsword received from the quest Black Knight's Fortress and found in the Black Knight's Fortress reward pack or created using a blacksmith's bench. The recipe is learned by acquiring the broken Titan's Wrath by defeating the Black Knight Titan. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
This weapon has three special effects: Its special attack is called Baptism of Fire, which deals damage and applies Burning to all enemies (and the player) within a 5 meter radius. Kills with this attack trigger Burning Execution which causes the weapon to become enchanted with fire magic, and further kills refresh the effect. However, this is an Enchanted Weapon, and additional enchantments cannot be cast on this weapon, whether Enchant Weapon: Fire or Enchant Weapon: Air.
This weapon has higher damage ranges than the shadow sword or other greatswords, but its incompatability with Enchant Weapon: Air means it misses out on the extra damage and attack speed from that enchantment. Similarly, Baptism of Fire is certainly cool, but Enchant Weapon: Fire is far easier to proc and maintain, and the forward momentum and spin of most other greatswords special actions will be hard to pass up.

(Journal) Lord Rasmodel has been put to rest at last.

He rarely knew quiet. His family pushed and cajoled him to further the Rasmodel name. Then he was beset by nightmares, as two malevolent beings grappled over his mind. When the Dreaming Stone shattered, they all took him. He was their spoils.

We can only hope that, when death came, there was quietus. He felt it for a moment as the Dreaming Stone fell, and - perhaps - he feels it on the journey over the Noumenon.

The part of him that was a titan - that part remains. You hold it in your hands. Unleash its wrath.

name: Toktz-Mej-Tal

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Forged from volcanic glass, its pointed tip bleeds fire as though the earth itself burns within. The heat never fades.

description:
The toktz-mej-tal is a power level 7 staff that can be crafted at a mystic forge. The recipe is unlocked after studying the elongated obsidian construct vestige, which can be dropped by KotHaar-Hur and KotHaar-Xil in Umbral Sands with a 2/100 drop rate. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is that it has an increased chance of landing critical strikes, although the exact chance is unknown. If it functions similarly to other weapons that have an extra chance to crit, then it would be 15%. However, it also has reduced durability, 300 less than other staves from Ghornfell, Fellhollow, and Umbral Sands, and 600 less than staves from Dowdun Reach.
With a rune damage multiplier of 8.4, it is 0.3 and 0.4 less than the staff of light and the necromancer's staff, respectively, when ascended to power level 7. However, as we have calculated with the draconic staff (which has 15% additional chance to crit), the multipliers would need to increase to 12.x for the increased chance to crit to provide an average increase in overall damage done. And again, although durability is trivial to manage with Magical Mending, the extended duration of the fight caves may warrant a different choice.

(Journal) Stone is not traditionally great at channelling magical energies. Stone is hard, solid and unchanging. Its shape can be carved away, but it will not bend, nor yield, only snap and crumble. Magic requires a more pliable medium to be used effectively.

Yet, the KotHaar are older creatures, to whom magic itself must bend. Creatures who were forged at the very birth of magic on Gielinor. The magic of the Elder Gods, to which all of creation must kneel.

This staff, the TokTz-Mej-Tal is older than the civilisations of Gielinor, and it still carries some of that old-world magic within it.

Try not to break it.

name: Toktz-Xil-Ak

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A double-pointed sword that is extremely efficient at finding the weak spots in your enemies.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
INCREASED chance of landing CRITICAL HITS
Reduced DURABILITY

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 10x Refined Obsidian, 5x Scorch Leather, 3x Desert Thread

description:
Toktz-xil-ak is a power level 7 melee weapon that can be unlocked by studying the shattered black blade (Umbral Sands) dropped by KotHaar-Kals with a 2/100 drop rate. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is a 2% increased critical strike chance, but a 25% decreased durability when compared to other adamant tier gear. Most other weapons that have an increased chance to crit like the Skullsplitter or dragonbone dagger increase the chance by 15%, so 2% is underwhelming.
That being said, this weapon has the same damage range as the wooden training sword and the black sword, and higher durability than the wooden training sword but lower than the black sword. The black sword therefore wins out when fighting mages, but even the adamant sword with 400 more durability might be considered over this sword for something like the Fight Caves as long as the benefit is only a mere 2% crit chance increase.

(Journal) A blade forged from obsidian, in the heart of a great volcano.

The KotHaar of Ashenfall are ancient beings, whose existence dates back millennia ago to when the elder gods first created the region. At the end of their lives, they would take themselves on long pilgrimages through underground tunnels, back to the mainland, where they would be reborn anew in the Elder Kiln.

Fuzan put a stop to that, by destroying those tunnels.

name: TzHaar-Ket-Om

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A massive warhammer of obsidian hue. Each swing carries the weight of something ancient.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- HITS cause BLEED build up on targets

- Reduced DURABILITY

description:
TzHaar-ket-om is a power level 7 two-handed warhammer that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. The recipe is unlocked after studying the bludgeoning obsidian construct, which can be dropped by KotHaar-Ket in Umbral Sands. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is that it builds up a Bleed effect on targets, dealing 56 damage after getting 5 hits in a short time, but it also has 25% reduced durability. There is also currently a known bug where it displays a combo of 21 and one where you cannot hit more than once on servers where you are not the host.
This weapon has the same damage range as an adamant warhammer, but its so much lower than the granite maul at power level 7 (196 - 283) even taking the Bleed damage into consideration that the granite maul is the clear choice of which two-handed warhammer to ascend.

(Journal) The KotHaar are practical creatures, not known for flights of fancy nor leaps of imagination. So, it makes sense that they would create a weapon like this.

The Tzhaar-Ket-Hom is a large cylinder of obsidian, whose purpose is to be whacked against something with as much force as one can muster. The impact delivers enough kinetic energy to split rock, shatter bone and do tremendous damage to ones internal organs.

Elegant this weapon is not, but you cannot argue with its efficiency.

name: Ulv's Longbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Once the bow of a silent hunter. Deals additional damage to unaware targets.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 12x Willow Logs, 8x Fine Thread, 10x Animal Bone, 4x Green Dragonhide Leather, 12x Dwellberries

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 6 / 82 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 100 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 118 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 138

description:
Ulv's longbow is a power level 5 longbow that can be obtained (as well as its crafting recipe) as a reward from the Mirror, Mirror quest. It can then be crafted from a fletching bench. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is 15% increased damage against unsuspecting targets, i.e. ones not yet in combat. Interestingly, this is the same damage bonus as trick shot, meaning that this weapon can deal the same damage on the first hit on a target as follow up trick shots on the same target.
Once the player can no longer continue aiming (to dodge an attack, for example), the trick shot is lost and another arrow will have to be fully drawn and fired to get it back. This makes the hunter stagbow's 10% faster draw speed more appealing, as it can loose and get back to trick shots faster. This weapon would be a competitive alternative, but after ascending to power level 7, the hunter stagbow far outpaces this weapon's base damage with 152 compared to only 100. Even with the special effect, the hunter stagbow will hit harder on every shot and is therefore the ideal longbow to ascend.

(Journal) Ulv was always the silent hunter, in more ways than one. While it was true that no word ever left his lips, his footsteps, breath and, most importantly, his arrows were all equally devoid of sound. The Wild Knights would jokingly call him the Silent Killer - though over time, the crueller among them called him Silent But Deadly - knowing he lacked the ability to argue back. The boy took these insults with quiet grace, never biting back, never reacting. He was used to such small cruelties, having faced them all his life.
He had carved the bow himself and once walked Ravanna through the process. The two of them had a true a friendship as could ever be hoped for. No linger romantic tensions. No transaction or debt. No honour chained them together. They were friends simply because they were. Because two lonely people had found each other and a comfort in the other's eccentricities. The wolf and the bat, platonic soulmates to the end.

For one of his birthdays, Ravanna enchanted the bow with a simple spell. She took animal bones, skulls and hides and wove necromantic magic through them, wrapping them around the limb and grip of the bow, imbuing them with just enough of the Underworld to strip them of their sound and a little of their substance. Like ghosts, the arrows would sail silently through the air, dropping targets that never knew what hit them.

It would have been the perfect birthday gift. If only Ulv had lived long enough to receive it.

The garou can be brutal in their assaults, considering notions like mercy to be the domain of the weak and cowardly. Ulv was simply in the wrong place at the wrong time. He was ambushed by a patrol of young garou looking for the bloodmark that would grant them adulthood. There were six of them; Ulv reduced their number to four before claws tore his through, silencing him forever.

When Ravanna found his body, she went mad. An anger unlike any other, a rage more powerful than any storm, waged a war of light and the dark inside her. The darkness won. Using the souls of the slain garou, Ravanna's necromantic curse tore through the Highlands, twisting the clouds into screaming things filled with a mere sliver of her rage. AS the ghosts of the dead garou crashed about within them, the clouds unleashed lightning and thunder upon the populace below, destroying countless settlements in an instant and countless more over the centuries that followed.

name: Undead Ranger's Bow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: This bow still fires with undeadly precision.

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 16x Undead Bone, 4x Fine Thread, 2x Steel Bar, 2x Sapphire, 6x Vault Shard

infobox.label: Upgrades
infobox.value: 6 / 61 / Ascension Core (Power Level 6) 1; 7 / 73 / Ascension Core (Power Level 7) 1; 8 / 85 / Ascension Core (Power Level 8) 1; 9 / 97

description:
The undead ranger's bow is a power level 5 shortbow that can be crafted at a fletching bench. The recipe is learned from a dragonkin effigy in Skekven Kara, the dragonkin vault in eastern Fellhollow. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is listed as increased damage but reduced durability. The reduced durability works as this weapon has 1,050 compared to the willow shortbow's 1300, however it has the same damage, both listed and actual.
It fires faster but deals the same damage as the crystal bow, which also has shattershot. However, the wild scout's shortbow has 10% faster draw speed with only 1-5% lower damage, increasing with higher power levels, making it the ideal shortbow to ascend.

(Journal) There was a villager in Emberwood called Holtz, who was a master with the bow. He could shoot rats from across a field and never scored less than a bullseye whenever he aimed for an archery target. Yet he had no desire for warfare, and no matter the words of encouragement from the captain, he would never join the guard.

For him, archery was a passion, an art, never to be used against another person. A stance quickly forgotten by his shambling corpse.

name: Wild Scout's Shortbow

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A bow used by a Wild Knight scout. Maintaining balance, one arrow at a time.

infobox.label: Special effect
infobox.value:
- Increased DRAW SPEED with RANGED ATTACKS

- Reduced DAMAGE

infobox.label: Recipe Materials
infobox.value: 10x Oak Logs, 2x Antler, 2x Wool Thread, 2x Dwellberries

infobox.label: Upgrades

description:
The wild scout's shortbow is a power level 3 shortbow that can be crafted at a fletching bench. The recipe is learned from a dragonkin effigy in Takla Kara, the dragonkin vault in central Fractured Plains. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is 10% increased draw speed, making this weapon draw faster than other shortbows. This does not affect quick actions.
The crystal bow and the undead ranger's bow have slightly higher base damage at all power levels, but they are supposed to have much higher base damage than they do (the undead ranger's bow's special effect is supposed to be increased damage after all), but they fire slower, the crystal bow especially so. They also have the same durability, which means that as long as the crystal bow's shattershot is not being used, then this weapon is the ideal shortbow to ascend.

(Journal) There was magic once, in this bow, though it has mostly faded now. Runes were ground down and mixed with plant oils to create a special resin that allowed the Wild Knights to work their magic through the bow, as if they were carrying runes. That magic has faded and the recipe for the mixture is lost to the ages, but these bows are still formidable in their own right.

Wild Knights told tales of creatures that lived within the wilds of Ashenfall and that could not be felled by normal bows. Deer with hides that glistened with starlight, sheep with silver fleeces repelled all arrows. They claimed that these magically infused bows were the only ones capable of harming the creatures, though none ever returned with trophies to share.

description:
The willow longbow is a power level 5 longbow that can be crafted from a fletching bench.

(Journal) Ulv had many skills, but hunting was his strongest. He was inherently quiet, still as the night, and he could hold his position, in the trees or bushes, for hours at a time. Ravanna was never good at this. When the two of them hunted together, Ravanna would sneeze, cough, or scream at the sight of an unexpected insect, and the two of them would watch their quarry disappear off into the night.
Although this would occasionally test their friendship, Ulv never really held it against Ravanna. Instead, he continued attempting to teach the necromancer the ways of the forest, and the techniques the Wild Knights would use to track down game. It never took. Try as she might, Ravanna was never going to be silent as a shadow.

In apology, she looked for a way to create a weapon that would reduce the impact of her noisy nature. Longbows fired further and faster, meaning that less stealth was needed. She made her way into Fellhollow in search of a material strong enough, and returned with willow branches that she crafted into a longbow as a gift for her friend.

Their hunts improved dramatically afterward. That was, until they became the hunted.

(Journal) As the dead rose in greater and greater numbers, the villagers needed stronger weapons to defeat them. Their ash and oak longbows failed to unleash sufficient force needed to stem the relentless tide of the undead. They needed a stronger material, that was also flexible enough to deliver arrows of great enough force.

Willow was their solution. It is said that the first willow shortbow was gifted to a villager by a spirit that dwelled within the grove. Legends say that the spirit had an unnatural beauty, and would lure foolish villagers into the waters where they would be drowned. Yet, somehow, one villager earned not the spirits ire, but their admiration.

The spirit gave up their immortal life, to court the villager. They brought gifts of flowers, fish and finally they gifted a shortbow made from the willow trees in the spirits grove. The validity of this tale is hotly debated, with most assuming it is little more than myth, yet willow groves are still considered spiritual places, where one must be careful who they talk to.

description:
The wolfbane dagger is a power level 5 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. The recipe is acquired from a dragonkin effigy found in Vekchenven Kara, the dragonkin vault in central Fellhollow. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is 25% increased damage against wolves, which includes wolves, dire wolves, dragonwolves, ghost wolves and hellhounds.
Although keris has 2 higher max hit at power level 7, this dagger when ascended has the same stats as the dragonbone dagger, and so when not attacking either kalphites or wolves, the dragonbone dagger is the ideal one-handed stabbing weapon to ascend.

(Journal) Vannaka knows this dagger only too well, for it was used against him every time he tried to prove his mettle against the other slayer masters. Although he would never willingly transform to prove his might, the unsettling sight of the dagger broke his morale enough to make him falter, and that was enough of an edge for his defeat.

description:
The wooden training sword is a power level 2 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a crafting table. The recipe is learned by consuming the an educational blade, found in a chest atop the eastern roof of the church in Temple Woods. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Unlike many other ascendable vestige and masterwork weapons and armour, this weapon does not have a special effect.
This means that when compared to other swords like the black sword or toktz-xil-ak, they will often be the better choices to ascend.

(Journal) In the village of Bramblemead, children grew up knowing battle. The God Wars hadn't reached them yet, but the priests always knew that danger was coming. So children were taught combat in the form of a game.

Carpenters were encouraged to make little wooden swords so that the children could emulate the noble paladins who wandered the village. These soldiers were held up as role models. Young men and women daydreamed through school of taking up those glittering swords and running off into adventure.

These weapons clicked and clacked against one another, seemingly harmless to the adults that watched. But wood in Bramblemead was hardened and preserved by druidic magic, and the damage these swords could deal soom became clear. Injuries were common, bruises and broken bones were the rite of passage of every child.

It was fortunate, perhaps, that these weapons were so painful — because the children of Bramblemead grew up with a better understanding that war was no game.

description:
Yew longbow is a power level 7 longbow.

(Journal) The hunter is the lifeblood of the Moon Garou. The Umbral Sands are not as hospitable to agriculture as many would like, so diets must be supplemented with fresh meat. This is particularly true for the Moon Garou, who remain primarily carnivorous in nature.

One hunter, Flytr, was the first to craft a longbow from the yew trees in the oases. Legend had it that the trees were sacred, special, a gift of the River Mother, designed to keep the Moon Garou safe. It was the greatest of blasphemies to use the wood for anything, but Flytr had never been particularly concerned with matters of faith.

She found a tree that had been struck by lightning, to lessen the guilt of repurposing the wood. She whittled down branch and bough, to create the longbow and, when she was done, she could have sworn the weapon was excited to be used.

It felled foes at great range, making her one of the best hunters the tribe had ever seen. Soon after, yew trees were no longer protected, as it came to be believed that the strength of the bow was proof that the River Mother wanted the wood to be used.

(Journal) Moon Garou scouts scour the desert armed with these bows. The sands obscure much until you’re right on top of it and so these bows are often more useful than the longer ranged weapons, against the dangers of the desert.

In the camps, the eldest garou will often teach the young cubs how to handle a shortbow. They will have the youngsters unleash a volley of arrows at clay pots, straw dolls, or cacti, and help train them to fire with greater accuracy.

Many of the young cubs will keep the shortbow with them as they grow into adulthood, using it as a decorative piece in their home -- a sign of a youth well spent, and a reminder that nothing lasts forever.

description:
The zamorak staff is a power level 6 staff that can be crafted with a mystic forge. This staff and its recipe are unlocked after completing What's Theirs is Mine!, the nodestone quest in Dowdun Reach. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect, Burning Ambition, increases burning damage caused by fire magic by 33%. At power level 6, that's an increase from 15 to 20 per tick, and at power level 7 an increase from 17 to 23 per tick. Burning damage ticks once every second for 6 seconds. This weapon's special action, Flames of Zamorak, uses 18 stamina and charges up an attack that then slams the staff down to cause a significant area of effect of damage that also instantly causes burning on enemies. This attack deals 18 base rune damage, or 123 damage (plus burning) at power level 6 with a rune damage modifier of 6.8 and 150 damage (plus burning) at power level 7 with a rune damage modifier of 8.3. However, due to the other effect, Elemental Imbalance, this weapon deals only half damage with air magic, water magic, and earth magic.
This staff is therefore incredibly powerful as long as only fire magic is being used. Even being 0.4 - 0.5 rune damage modifier lower than the staff of light and necromancer's staff, the burning damage will surpass the rune damage. Not to mention, the special action deals an exceptional amount of damage all around the user, instantly burning enemies as well, which covers a staff's weakness when multiple enemies get close. However, using any other form of magic is a significant damage loss, and unfortunately a number of enemies are resistant to fire and burning (like the knights and mages of Dowdun Reach) or completely immune (like the KotHaar). Assuming one can manage the weight and inventory slot, taking this staff for fire magic and another for the others is a viable strategy. Also, although the fire cape doesn't have great synergy (since it requires blocking or taking damage to cause burning and only melee kills on burning targets restore stamina), the zamorak cape on the other hand will cause Afterimage to explode, for those mages with a penchant for explosives.

(Journal) There are myths and anecdotes about Zamorak appearing to the inhabitants of Dowdun Reach. Few truly believe them. Zamorak is not one for hiding his presence: he's more theatrical than that.

It may be hard to believe, but some have tried to 'summon' Zamorak to Dowdun Reach. Call it the hubris of a demon summoner: a student feels they have mastered the art of summoning demons, so believes the next rung on the ladder is god. Never mind that Zamorak has no ounce of demon within him.

Zamorak can be accused of many things, but he does have a sense of humour. These attempts have been greeted with a gift. He has been known to kick a bloodveld through the portal, or another creature he has to hand. It gives the demon summoner a little spot-test.

description:
The zombie arm is a power level 4 melee weapon that is awarded to the player after completing The Great Body Robbery, and can then be crafted using a blacksmith's bench. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores. 
It is not clear what this weapon's special effect is as its "electrifying properties" are ambiguous. When a player receives the Shocked debuff, their stamina is completely drained, but since enemies do not have stamina, and as there are no visible effects or extra damage done, it does not appear to do anything to them. It also does not seem to prevent the player or cause enemies to be struck by lightning.
It has the same damage values and attack style as the Skullsplitter, so that weapon's +15% critical strike chance is better, but the higher base damage and additional slash damage of the zombie axe wins out overall when considering weapons to ascend.

(Journal) Let us dwell, for a moment, on the original owner of this club, a man named Mort. Mortimer Grimm had the sort of name adored by those who believe in nominative determinism. Mort Grimm, his parents effectively cursed him at birth to become an undead monstrosity, and their curse came true.

The undead were rare in Ghornfell, but not unheard of. Some druids, who spent too long in the Whispering Swamps, apparently learned strange rituals that would raise a corpse as a mindless servant, doomed to wander the world in search of delicious, delicious brains. Mort was one of these, though he resurrected with somewhat less all-consuming-hunger than his cohorts. As the other zombies were herded towards human encampments, Mort wandered off into the poisonous Bloodblight Swamp, in search of mysteries. There he encountered a strange scientist who did not immediately attempt to set him on fire – an improvement over the response from most people.

This would begin a truer friendship than Mort thought possible. Whilst, yes, the scientist could never remember Mort's name and insisted on calling him Igor. And, yes, Mort would spend much of his time listening to lectures on why everyone else is stupid, whilst carrying large and disturbingly-shaped bags of unknown contents, for the scientist. Still, they would laugh and they would watch the sunsets together, and for the first time in a long time, Mort was happy.

Until the scientist asked Mort to build the lightning conductor. One flash of inspiration later, and Mort's tragic existence reduced itself to this somewhat sinister club.

Still, waste not want not, I always say.

description:
The zombie axe is a power level 5 one-handed melee weapon that can be crafted at a blacksmith's bench. The axe and its recipe are received by completing Doric's Quest. It can be ascended at the mystic forge using ascension cores.
Its special effect is that it deals both crush and slash damage simultaneously. Both damage types are taken into account when considering monsters' weaknesses and resistances. This weapon is effective against enemies that are weak to crush but not resistant to slash (including vault guardians, putrid rats, garou thanes, skeletal marauders, and skeletal necromancers). However, against enemies that are weak to crush but resistant to slash damage (including skeletal hoplites, zogres, black knight guardians, black knight warriors, and the black knight titan), this weapon will deal slightly less damage to them because resistances lower damage (-33%) more than weaknesses increase it (+25%). Note that this damage is additive rather than multiplicative, unlike other damage modifiers (i.e. it will lower damage by a factor of 0.92 rather than 0.8375).
This weapon has a higher base damage than other similar one-handed crush weapons, but that benefit is lost against enemies that are also resistant to slash, making Skullsplitter with its +15% critical strike chance more valuable. This weapon also uses the mace moveset, which hits slower than the sword, scimitar, or whip move set, therefore against enemies that are weak to slash but not resistant to crush (including abyssal demons, lost souls, zombies, Zamorakian acolytes, and mages of zamorak), weapons like the black sword, Imaru's talon, or abyssal whip may be better choices.

(Trivia) A similar variant of the zombie axe is found in Old School RuneScape, where it is dropped by a Armoured Zombie in Zemouregal's Fort or Base.
The axe shares a similar appearance to that of its Old School RuneScape, but remains unique in certain parts, such as the skull and detailed design.

(Journal) Captain Artorius Flamhanger was a brave man, who stood against the rampaging forces of the damned even as his defences crumbles around him. He never wavered, never faltered, and never left a man behind.
In a better world, there would be songs about him. But Fellhollow scorns legacy, leaving only ruins and despair where hope might take root.

He held the line against the encroaching horde far longer than anywhere else in the region. Days turned into months and months grew into years. As the rest of the region vanished into death, despair and rot, Captain Flamhanger stood strong. As his children died and rose again, the captain returned them to the earth with sombre compassion. when his wife joined them in death, he gave her a final kiss of polished silver that cleaved her head from her shoulder.

In a better world he might have held back the darkness, stood as a single ray of light in a world of shadow. But this is not our world. There are no sages of this man, no great texts telling of his heroic deeds. The only sound he made in the time after his death, is the bubbling song of digestive acids within a zogre's belly.

History is penned by the survivors and the victors, yet the deeds of the dead echo across time. This axe, simple as it may appear, is infused with vengeance against the dead that had taken so much from a good man.
